title: Account Specialist, Urology - Chicago, IL
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Account Specialist role promotes a product to community practices and health systems. Customer accounts may include community/private practices, community-based hospitals, academic medical centers, and government accounts (military treatment facilities and/or Veteran’s Affairs Medical Centers). The Account Specialist develops and maintains relationships with various accounts/departments such as neurology, pain medicine, physical medicine and rehabilitation, primary care, and pharmacy. Or in Urology, specialists such as urology, urogynecology, obstetrics and gynecology, female pelvic medicine, ambulatory surgical centers, and reconstructive surgery.
Responsibilities
Promote a product to meet/exceed sales goals in community/private practices as well as hospitals/health systems.
Identify/uncover customer needs (training, clinical, operational, reimbursement) and address with appropriate AbbVie resources
Provide education and clinical/injection training for residents, fellows, and other key hospital personnel.
Expert delivery of anatomical/procedural information and training, including the appropriate use of anatomical terminology to train injection paradigms/postures while highlighting various anatomical and injection insights and considerations.
Effectively utilize AbbVie's sales and data resources to enhance productivity and growth of AbbVie products while implementing U.S. Marketing Plan.
Collaborate with other Account Specialist to promote the product for approved indications and execute individual, department, or group resident/fellow trainings within hospital/health system accounts.
Bachelor’s degree in health, sciences, pharmacy or business-related field preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required.
Relevant and equivalent industry experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree is at least five (5) years of technical experience with three (3) or more years of experience within sales preferred and a high school diploma/GED required
Experience with Buy & Bill and/or Specialty Pharmacy products is preferred, in both health systems and private practice
Ability to lift/pull 25–100 lb. training models and meet necessary hospital credentialing/vaccination requirements
Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements
Ability to travel adequately to cover territory, as well as overnight attendance at scheduled training events and sales meetings
Documented history of strong sales performance, preferably in a clinical/technical/consultative sales role with multiple decision makers is preferred. Ability to manage a complex sell, learn procedural, technical, clinical, and anatomical information quickly and communicate/present/train to a variety of audiences
An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials.
These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases, fingerprinting and specific licenses required by individual state or cities. Please remember that you are solely responsible for ensuring that you satisfy all HCIR credentialing requirements and for any associated liability for failing to do so. AbbVie has resources available to you to help answer questions you may have.

description:

The Medical Affairs (MA) organization provides patients, healthcare providers and payers everywhere with the practical and clinically relevant information and solutions they need to use AbbVie products safely and effectively, throughout the product lifecycle and the patient’s journey.
The Scientific Director / Medical Director provides medical and scientific input into strategic and operational medical affairs activities for AbbVie’s Ovarian Cancer portfolio such as: health-care professional and provider interactions (Payers, Patients, Prescribers, and Providers); generation of clinical and scientific data (enhancing therapeutic benefit and value); educational initiatives (medical education, data, guidelines, and value proposition); safeguarding patient safety (risk minimization activities and safety surveillance activities).
Works closely with commercial teams to provide strategic medical input into core brand (product) strategies and may support medical and marketing activities (promotional material generation and product launches) and market access. Collaborates with clinical development on Medical Affairs support of priority trials.
This position can be based at the following locations and will follow a hybrid model of 3 days/week onsite: Mettawa, IL; Florham Park, NJ; Irvine, CA; San Francisco, CA.
Responsibilities
Initiates medical affairs activities, generation and dissemination of data supporting the Ovarian Cancer scientific strategy
Provides scientific/medical education to all relevant internal stakeholders related to our Ovarian Cancer portfolio
Develops and executes Medical Affairs support of priority clinical development trials.
Contributes to the development of and leads the execution of the Medical Education / Advisory Board & EE Engagement Plan generation in line with TA plan. Lead the individual (Global) Conference planning and execution.
Generates clinical and scientific data per evidence gap assessment.
Acts as a clinical interface and actively solicits opinion through leader interactions related to the molecule and disease area; partners with international Medical Affairs, Commercial and other functions in these activities as required, consistent with corporate policies, to ensure that broad cross-functional perspectives are incorporated into Clinical Development Plans and protocols as appropriate.
May be responsible for performing the accurate and detailed medical review of complex advertising and promotional materials for assigned therapeutic area(s) within Medical Affairs. Provides timely and accurate reviews of promotional materials in accordance with established policies and practice standards, including regulatory guidelines to meet customer needs.
May interact with and coordinates appropriate scientific and medical activities with internal stakeholders (i.e. commercial, clinical operations, discovery, statistics, regulatory, etc.) as they relate to on-going medical affairs projects.
May assist as consultant and liaison with other corporations when working under licensing agreements and/or in the evaluation of new business development opportunities.
Represents AbbVie at external meetings including investigator meetings, scientific association meetings, etc.
Ensures budgets, timelines, compliance requirements are factored into programs' scientific activities.
Scientific Director: Bachelor’s Degree in the sciences. Advanced Degree PhD, PharmD, PA or NP preferred. Residency or additional post doctorate experience preferred.
5-7+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry or equivalent; substantial understanding of relevant therapeutic area required.
Medical Director: Medical Doctorate (M.D.) degree or equivalent (D.O. or non-US equivalent of M.D.). Relevant therapeutic specialty in an academic or hospital environment preferred. Completion of residency and/or fellowship preferred.
0-2+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry or equivalent.
Knowledge of clinical trial methodology, regulatory requirements governing clinical trials and experience in the design of protocols preferred.
May have performed protocol design in the academic environment and/or acted as an assistant PI.
Interactions normally require the ability to gain cooperation of others, conduct presentations of technical information concerning specific projects and schedules, etc.
Ability to interact externally and internally to support global business strategy. Must possess excellent oral and written communication skills.
Works with some supervision and guidance. Exercises judgment within well-defined practices and policies.

title: Data Protection Specialist
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Data Protection Specialist works with various internal and external groups to ensure that AbbVie information security policies, practices, and procedures are properly implemented within AbbVie. They support the Data Protection Office in strengthening company data security controls and maturing operational processes. The individual will interface with a wide variety of people from different internal organizational units, interface with organizational personnel and staff to ensure that the policy is understood by those required to implement, monitor, and enforce the policy. This role is designed for a professional with an engineering, computer science, software development, or related technical background who is interested in the business, governance, and assurance aspects of data security. Under the guidance of the Data Protection Office, the role will drive control auditing, assurance activities, governance, development, security logging, automation, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence to improve efficiency, consistency, and maturity of data protection processes.
Responsibilities:
Establish and maintain strong relationships with IT and Business group leaders to understand goals, programs, and plans. Evaluate and articulate program security requirements; identify potential security risk factors and business impact.
Conduct assessments of controls to ensure data protection controls are in place.
Leverage AI to analyze volumes of data across File Labeling, Application logs, and infrastructure datasets to automate control assurance.
Engage AbbVie Third Party Vendors to assess security posture, remediation requirements, and compensating controls as they apply to Business Applications.
Develop in-depth knowledge of AbbVie Information Security policies, processes, and procedures, as well as compliance processes and initiatives to provide subject matter expertise and guidance to other organizations (Commercial, R&D, Audit, Legal, Purchasing, etc.) within AbbVie in these matters.
Provide Information Security expertise and guidance to Business group leaders and IT Owners to ensure an appropriate balance between security risks and business enablement for identified business programs and initiatives.
Provide reporting to management on potential Data Privacy risks and planned remediation.
Act as point of contact regarding Information Security matters and AbbVie security policies for AbbVie Purchasing, Legal/Privacy and Quality.
Review current technology and information policies and practices for continued applicability with respect to AbbVie commercial and R&D business programs. Provide recommendations for improvements.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree with 5 years of experience; OR Master's Degree with 4 years of experience in Information Security, Data Privacy, or IT Compliance experience.
Familiarity with, and experience using, a variety of information security control frameworks, including, but not limited to: NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 2700X, PCI-DSS, SWIFT, Cloud Controls Matrix, HITRUST, NIST 800-171, CIS Controls, etc.
Familiarity with global and regional Data Privacy regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, and CCPA.
Experience aligning and testing information security controls and frameworks.
Experience writing policies and procedures.
Experience working in information security or data privacy in a large, global organization.
Strong project management, collaboration, communication, and organizational skills.
Adept at communicating concepts to diverse audiences with varying skill sets.
Strong written and verbal communication skills are critical.
Preferred:
Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified Information Privacy Technologist (CIPT), or other equivalent certifications preferred.
​Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law: ​
The compensation range described below is the range of possible base pay compensation that the Company believes in good faith it will pay for this role at the time of this posting based on the job grade for this position. Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits including paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick), medical/dental/vision insurance and 401(k) to eligible employees.​
This job is eligible to participate in our short-term incentive programs. ​

The  Head of Patient Advocacy and Professional Societies Engagement - Oncology  leads the global strategy for building, managing, and sustaining authentic, high-impact relationships with cancer patient advocacy organizations (PAOs), professional oncology societies, and key policy stakeholders.
This leadership role will embed a patient-centric mindset across the Global Oncology Medical Affairs enterprise. will ensure the patient voice shapes clinical pathways across our robust portfolio of Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs), T-Cell Engagers (TCEs), and targeted small molecules.  Will manage, mentor, and develop a high-performing global team of 4 direct reports focused entirely on the hematology and solid tumor landscape.
Position will be based from an AbbVie major R&D site and follow a hybrid model of 3 days/week on-site. Locations include Mettawa, IL (headquarters), Florham Park, NJ, Waltham, MA, San Francisco, CA, and Irvine, CA.
Key Responsibilities
Global Strategy & Pipeline Integration:  Design and execute the multi-year global engagement strategy for oncology PAOs aligned with AbbVie’s core therapeutic focus areas, spanning  Hematologic Malignancies  (CLL, AML, DLBCL, Multiple Myeloma) and  Solid Tumors  (NSCLC, SCLC, Ovarian Cancer, Colorectal Cancer).
Modality-Specific Advocacy:  Develop specialized, tailored patient engagement frameworks for next-generation modalities, capturing patient and caregiver insights unique to  Topoisomerase I inhibitor (Top1i)–based ADCs  and immune-based pipelines.
Team Leadership & Development:  Lead, mentor, and scale a team of 4 direct reports, fostering a culture of compliance, clinical fluency, and cross-functional collaboration in the complex global oncology space.
Clinical Trial Co-Creation:  Partner with clinical development to leverage patient organization insights to optimize trial designs, decentralized trial models, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for late-stage and registrational pipeline assets.
Professional Oncology Alliances:  Cultivate strategic partnerships with primary global professional organizations (such as  ASCO, ESMO, ASH, WCLC, and SGO ) to advance scientific exchange, consensus-building, and independent medical educational grants.

Exceptional interpersonal, diplomacy, and executive communication skills.
Demonstrated commitment to driving health equity and reducing disease awareness gaps in underserved cancer patient populations.

title: Senior Manager, Payer Contract Analytics
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Senior Manager, Payer Contract Analytics, will independently lead contract modeling and deal scenario strategy for AbbVie's key PBM and payer customers across Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid channels. This role evaluates contract scenarios to clearly articulate AbbVie’s differentiated clinical value to payers while protecting branded product net price and preferred market access positions.
This role combines expertise in contract modeling, predictive analytics, trend measurement, and financial reporting, and partners closely with Marketing, Finance, field-based Account Managers, and IT. The Senior Manager ensures AbbVie has the pricing and deal analytics needed to secure preferred formulary access at the right cost, managing cost-of-access risk for in-line and pipeline products and setting the standard for contract modeling excellence.
This role reports to the Director, Immunology Contract Analytics.
Key Job Responsibilities
Contract Modeling and Deal Strategy
Serve as the primary contract modeling lead for assigned brands and therapeutic areas with a primary focus on AbbVie’s Immunology portfolio of brands.  Independently quantify the financial and long-range planning impact of national and regional PBM and payer contracts under different market access scenarios.
Lead breakeven projections and gross-to-net evaluations of proposed contracts, identifying the rebate and access terms that secure preferred formulary position.
Lead payer RFP modeling reviews with Account Managers, Finance, and Payer Strategy teams. Agree on modeling assumptions and key sales drivers early to improve forecast precision and speed up bid turnaround.
Evaluate non-rebate contract terms, such as administrative fees, price protection, rebate guarantees, utilization management criteria, and biosimilar step-edit provisions, for their effect on net price and access durability.
Insights and Executive Communication
Turn modeling outcomes into executive-level narratives and recommendations that inform deal budgets and approval decisions. Serve as a trusted advisor, making sure competitive bid responses are evidence-based and reflect current market dynamics.
Monitor payer and PBM contracting trends across Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid channels, and independently answer contracting analysis questions from senior stakeholders.
Post-Deal Performance Evaluation
Run post-deal retrospectives that compare actual and forecasted financials and recalibrate contract models and assumptions as needed.
Early Warning Performance Monitoring: Track contract performance KPIs (volume, share, net price, and forecast variance) through business-facing reporting tools, and flag accounts that are underperforming against their deal terms.
Contract Analytics Capability Development and Talent Coaching
Advance contracting analytics capabilities with APEX teams, vendor partners, and internal technical work groups. This includes AI-enabled scenario modeling, gross-to-net forecasting, scenario-specific demand analogues, key-driver sensitivity analyses, patient flow and flow-back modeling, sequential response simulations, time-to-event estimates, and competitor brand lifecycle event dynamics.
Manage external analytics vendors to deliver high-quality, timely insights using analytical approaches suited to each contracting scenario question.
Develop and mentor Payer Contract Analytics talent to strengthen pre- and post-deal insight generation that advance each brand's gross-to-net objectives over time.
The individual in this role should have the following background:
Must have a Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Economics, Actuarial Science, Business Analytics or a highly related field of study and 7+ years of work experience in financial modeling and/ or data analytics in the pharmaceutical, health care or other industry.
Alternatively, would accept a Masters in the same disciplines and 5+ years of work experience in financial modeling and/ or data analytics in the pharmaceutical, health care or other industry.
Strong business and financial acumen – prior experience in pharmaceutical contracting analyses with an emphasis on data and financial analysis is highly desirable.
A working knowledge and understanding of the ever-evolving pharmacy channel stakeholder economics, including Payers, Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs).
Demonstrated experience analyzing syndicated claims data sets (for example, IQVIA LAAD or Symphony Health) and formulary status data (for example, MMIT) for Pharmacy channel products.
Advanced Excel/VBA modeling skills, proficiency in SQL and/or Python, and experience building Microsoft Power BI dashboards.
Applied experience with forecasting and statistical methods, such as Bayesian methods, analogue-uptake curves, decision tree models, parametric hazard models, Monte Carlo simulations, and time-series forecasting.
Experience leading market assessments across biosimilar competition, 340B duplicate discount scrubbing on commercial rebate payments, PBM vertical integration fee schedules, and IRA policy impact on Medicare Part D contracting.
A proven ability to turn complex scenario-based analyses into clear executive recommendations that influence market access contract strategy decisions.

description:

The Partner QA Lead is the Airbnb Quality owner for the Elevated Support service tier across a portfolio of Community Support BPO partner sites. Working across partner QA teams, this role makes sure that each site scores interactions consistently, calibrates to the same standard as Airbnb, and turns what it finds into insight that Delivery and Partners can act on.
The Difference You Will Make:
Elevated Support is Airbnb's newest Community Support service tier, built for guests with urgent, complex or high-stakes issues. Cases are identified by an Elevated decisioning model, routed to a dedicated pool of specialized Specialists across voice, async and back-office queues, and supported around the clock by partner sites in multiple regions and languages. Its north-star metric is NPS, case resolution, cost per case, and reopen rate. Because the tier is new, its quality targets, scorecard and evaluation approach are still maturing, and this role helps set them.
The Partner QA Lead is paired with a Delivery (Ops) counterpart: Quality owns the standard, the evidence and the diagnosis, and Delivery and Quality partner on actions.
This is a hands-on, partner-facing execution role and a subject matter expert on Airbnb's quality standards. The Partner QA Lead is responsible for making the Quality program work on the ground: holding partner QA teams accountable, running calibration on the Lead With Hospitality (LWH) COPC form, diagnosing behavior opportunities before the weekly business reviews, and driving actions to address issues and opportunities for guests with urgent, high-stakes needs. The role works closely with the Quality Leads, other Partner QA Leads, Delivery, Training, Knowledge Management, the Elevated Support program team and Business Process Improvement (BPI), and is expected to become an expert in new standards and tools, such as Lead With Hospitality (LWH) QA framework and Observe.AI, and then to drive adoption across its partners.
A Typical Day:
Partner Quality Program Execution
Own the day-to-day execution of the Quality program for the Elevated Support service tier and the corresponding partner sites, languages and queues (voice, async and back office), including weekly QA evaluation targets, evaluation completeness, and coaching activity within your portfolio.
Validate performance data before every business review (WBR, MBR, QBR): confirm that partner QA scores are complete, accurate and comparable, then explain week-over-week movements in a short, clear narrative that Delivery and partner leadership can act on.
Run the Quality portion of each partner's operating cadence: weekly QA syncs, a pre-sync with your ROM/POM before each WBR, and the monthly and quarterly business reviews.
Partner Governance & Accountability
Hold partner QA teams to the Partner Scorecard: evaluation completeness, calibration accuracy, coaching effectiveness and actionable insights. Document gaps and agree action plans with owners and dates.
Audit the auditors: sample and re-score partner evaluations to confirm they follow the standard, and escalate sustained performance gaps to the Quality Lead.
Support new partner site onboarding, language expansion and site visits, making sure each new Elevated Support site and cohort is certified and calibrated to Airbnb standards before it scales, including interim QA coverage by experienced partner QAs while a new site stands up its own team.
Calibration & LWH Standards
Run calibration sessions across your Elevated Support partner sites on the LWH form, including evaluations scored at case level across every Specialist who touched the case, and track alignment at attribute and causal-factor level, so that quality is measured the same way regardless of partner or geography.
Support partner Team Lead calibration, including the weekly sessions that Partner Quality runs within each site, so Team Leads coach specialists in the same language as Quality.
Triage partner feedback on the form and recommend scoring guide updates through the Calibration DRI. Quality owns the standard; partners do not change it locally.
Insights, NPS Detractor Analysis & Escalation
Lead NPS detractor analysis, including the Global Detractor Analysis (GDA) framework, for Elevated Support, where NPS is the north-star metric. Correlate QA results with NPS, reopen rate, AQS and other operational KPIs, and point partner QA effort toward the sites, languages and case types that need it most.
Partner with Delivery, WFM and the Elevated Support program team to establish and refine QA targets and the tier scorecard, using LWH data to recommend realistic, evidence-based targets (for example where sites report they cannot reach targets carried over from volume tiers) and to monitor early-life performance of new sites and cohorts.
Validate the Elevated model end to end: sample cases to confirm the right cases are being identified and escalated to the tier, that handoffs and transfers (including to Premium Support and language queues) work as intended, and that the tier is staffed and routed so guests reach an Elevated Specialist.
Deep-dive repeat trends and build the business case for them. Route issues by type: tactical issues (coaching, site issues fixable with Learning Loft content) go to partner QA teams and Delivery, and macro issues go to OneTrack with an evidence pack, together with your ROM/POM.
Give partner QA teams and Delivery the data they need to find root cause: by partner, site, Specialist cohort, Specialist quartile and contact reason.
Share best practices with other Partner QA Leads, and cover for peers or the Quality Lead during staffing gaps, including language or regional coverage and short rotations.
Tools, Reporting & Cross-Functional Rollouts
Drive adoption of Observe.AI across your Elevated Support partner sites, including AutoQA review and annotation, access and permission hygiene, and the transition from interim evaluation forms to Observe.AI.
Be an expert on every new Quality initiative, such as LWH, Global Detractor Analysis, and Specialist Investigation Skills, and cascade it to your partners with clear expectations, training and follow-up.
Represent Quality for Elevated Support in cross-functional working groups (Product, program management, Knowledge Management, Training, Workforce and Routing) as the single point of contact for your partners, and make sure quality findings that point to policy, workflow or product gaps are raised, not left as coaching notes.
Protect partner QA capacity for strategic work such as deep dives and root-cause analysis, rather than ad hoc requests that are outside agreed scope.
Your Expertise:
6+ years of experience in Community or Customer Support Quality, Operations or a related field, including direct experience with QA programs across BPO or partner networks and experience supporting high-touch, escalated or premium service tiers.
Bachelor's Degree, preferably in related field required.
Demonstrated experience driving partner accountability: running calibration sessions, reviewing partner QA scorecards, and writing and following through on improvement plans with BPO QA teams.
Working knowledge of COPC methodology or an equivalent governance model: sampling requirements, calibration, and objective, behavior-based scoring forms.
Strong analytical skills: able to read weekly QA and KPI data (NPS, CSAT, iSAT, reopen rate, cost per case), diagnose the cause of score movements, and turn it into a clear narrative for Delivery and partner leadership.
Experience with QA platforms such as Observe.AI, or equivalent, including calibration management, form use and review of automated or AI-assisted scoring.

title: Head of Emerging Technology Strategy & Partnerships
description:
Imagine what you could do here. The people here at Apple don’t just create products — they create the kind of wonder that’s revolutionized entire industries. It’s the diversity of those people and their ideas that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do, from amazing technology to industry-leading environmental efforts. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it.
Apple’s Sales organization generates the revenue needed to fuel our ongoing development of products and services. This in turn, enriches the lives of hundreds of millions of people around the world. Our sales team, is in many ways, the face of Apple to our largest customers.
We are seeking a Head of Emerging Technology Strategy & Partnerships to decide where Apple places its next bets in the enterprise and AI ecosystem — and to build the team that turns those bets into adopted, repeatable business. This is a working manager role: you will personally originate and run a portfolio of strategic partnerships and market activation plans for Apple's highest-priority emerging technology initiatives, while building and coaching a team that runs the same playbook with increasing independence. No other platform company can pair this kind of ecosystem reach with Apple's architecture for privacy, security, and on-device intelligence — your job is to turn that architectural advantage into a commercial one, continuously, as hybrid AI redraws what partners and customers expect.
Because these partnerships are won on technology, you're a fit if you can go deep with engineers and architects on how it works and why it differentiates, and carry that substance into a funded, resourced, measurable commercial motion with C-suite leaders. You also bring the people instincts to grow a team of originators rather than just carry the portfolio yourself. We're looking for someone with big ideas who also knows how to get things built, funded, and shipped — a rare combination, and the core of this role.
As the Head of Emerging Technology Strategy & Partnerships, you will personally own a set of strategic initiatives and partnership pursuits end-to-end, while leading a team that owns equivalent portfolios across other emerging technology initiatives — from market activation and ecosystem engagement to technical solutioning and go-to-market design. As a working manager, you'll balance hands-on deal leadership with accountability for the people doing the same work: setting direction, developing capability, and ensuring the team operates as a high-performing, well-coached unit.
In this role, you will:
- Shape the How of Strategic Initiatives: Translate Apple's emerging technology bets into concrete market activation plans: the ecosystem required to pull the Apple platform through, the early adopters positioned to become lighthouse customers, and the enabling technologies and integrations needed to get there. You decide the motions, not just the destination — and you're accountable for measurable outcomes, not activity.
- Own a Working Portfolio: Personally originate, qualify, negotiate, and activate a dedicated set of strategic partnerships across enterprise platforms, AI frontier labs, and industry-specific ISVs — engaging daily with senior leaders and technical decision-makers across that ecosystem. Your own deals set the standard and the playbooks your team is expected to run.
- Solution Technology Win-Wins with Partners: Technology is what wins these partnerships, not relationships alone. Each is a win-win anchored in a specific product or platform advantage, and you'll solution it hands-on with partner and Apple engineers: evaluating integration architectures, finding the gaps, and defining the software enhancements on both sides that unlock adoption. Carry what you learn into Apple's product and platform roadmap discussions with clear technical rationale and business impact, and hold your team to the same standard — every partnership rests on a technology thesis, not just a commercial one.
- Build Apple's Differentiated Advantage: Architect joint value propositions and go-to-market strategies that establish clear, differentiated advantage through Apple's platform — on-device AI, security, and privacy architecture — and the ecosystem around it. Articulate precisely where Apple's silicon, OS, and services differentiate from alternatives, and translate that into what a partner gains by building on Apple. As hybrid AI becomes the defining lever in enterprise technology, continuously evolve Apple's partner value proposition, and your team's skill set, to keep that advantage expanding.
- Architect Repeatable Motions: Turn one-off wins into frameworks: partner qualification criteria (including technical fit and integration readiness), joint business planning models, reference architectures, and go-to-market plays (co-sell, co-marketing, enablement, pipeline development) that scale beyond any single relationship and beyond any single deal you personally run.
- Lead, Coach, and Scale the Team: Set team direction and goals aligned to organizational priorities. Coach and develop direct reports through regular 1:1s, feedback, and career planning — including building their technical depth in Apple's platform and in partner technologies. Manage performance — calibrating against expectations and addressing gaps directly and with empathy. Make hiring decisions and build a diverse, high-caliber team. Allocate team resources and workstreams across origination, technical solutioning, enablement, and commercial negotiation to balance coverage, individual growth, and your own portfolio commitments.
- Represent the Function Cross-Functionally: Partner closely with Industry Leadership, Enterprise/Partner Sales, Product Marketing, Engineering, and Operations to keep partnerships strategically aligned and measurably impactful — representing your team's priorities, resourcing needs, and development in those forums.
- Measure and Evolve: Track partner-sourced pipeline, revenue, and activation metrics. Monitor competitive and industry trends to keep strategy current. Use both to decide what to double down on, what to pause, and where the next emerging technology bet should go.
Minimum qualifications: 12+ years in business development, strategic partnerships, or ecosystem development within enterprise technology, with a track record of originating and activating partnerships that drove measurable go-to-market outcomes — not just relationship management.
8+ years of people management experience, including setting goals, coaching, managing performance, and making hiring decisions for a team.

Proven track record of leading cross-functional initiatives that have successfully transformed state-of-the-art computer vision research into production-ready features.
Deep product mindset focused on architecting technical solutions that solve real business problems and deliver high customer value.

title: Sr. Software Engineer - Distributed Storage
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds and provides systems that power many of Apple’s customer-facing services - including iCloud, iTunes, Siri and Maps. We deliver the core infrastructure primitives that enable teams across Apple to build services our customers rely on every day.
This is a ground-up effort to build a highly reliable, self-managing and scalable storage layer that can support exabyte-scale data and diverse access patterns. This new layer will also serve as the foundation for adopting and optimizing next-generation storage devices, enabling Apple to leverage emerging drive technologies with new performance and density characteristics. If you enjoy designing distributed systems that operate as a cohesive storage fabric, we want to hear from you.
We are creating a unified storage abstraction layer that will serve as the foundational layer for Apple’s distributed object, block, and future file storage systems. This new layer will provide a consistent API, common metadata model, scalable data distribution and high-performance IO path for workloads running in Apple Cloud.
Engineers on this team will work on the core of a unified storage layer designed to manage data objects, placement, redundancy and IO operations across thousands of nodes. You will help define the fundamental building blocks that unify different storage backends—object, block and future file interfaces—behind a single, extensible abstraction.
You will design consistent metadata services, build scalable data distribution algorithms, implement robust replication and fault-recovery mechanisms, and develop client-side libraries and protocols that expose a uniform interface to workloads across Apple.
Each component is being designed to support self-healing behaviors, automatic rebalancing and high-throughput, low-latency access paths.
We are looking for engineers who enjoy building foundational storage systems, solving complex distributed coordination challenges, and shaping a platform that will underpin Apple’s cloud storage strategy for many years.
Minimum qualifications: Strong problem-solving skills rooted in data structures, distributed systems, and concurrency.
7+ years of professional experience building and operating distributed systems.

title: Deployment Engineer (Field Operations)
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As our Deployment Engineer, you are the technical expert and central lifeline for our field crews. You are the voice of Base from mission control, providing end-to-end guidance to ensure every battery installation and service call is safe, efficient, and successful. This is not a typical support role. You’ll be the interdisciplinary link between our field electricians, our engineers, and our members, using tools like Grafana and Retool to monitor system health while troubleshooting issues over the phone, text, and Slack. This role offers a unique opportunity to develop a 360-degree view of our technology. 



You’ll gain real-world expertise in hardware, software, and field operations, all while contributing directly to the improvement of our product and deployment playbooks. This role is best suited for a tech-savvy experienced engineer who enjoys solving complex problems in real-time or for a fast-learning generalist that can flex into any scope and excel. Over time, this position could grow into potential field leadership, operations, or engineering roles.



What You'll Do

 - Typical week: ~75% of your time live-supporting (from our HQ in Austin, TX) field crews during installations and service calls; ~25% analyzing issues, updating playbooks, and collaborating with other teams.

 - Provide end-to-end guidance and troubleshooting for battery installations and service calls over phone, text, and Slack.

 - Serve as the first line of technical support for in-field electrical questions and hardware issues, escalating complex compliance issues and documenting new solutions.

 - Identify field issue trends over time and flag high impact issues to hardware, software, or deployment teams.

 - Work closely with Member Experience to ensure the best possible experience for our members.

 - Create and maintain troubleshooting aid and hardware defect logs.

 - Create, track, and close service tickets through Jira or Odoo.

 - You’ll directly impact installation speed, safety, and uptime while your insights will shape our hardware roadmap and operating procedures.
   
   

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years in a technical support, electrical, or IT troubleshooting role.

 - Strong foundation in electrical concepts; licensed electrician or hands-on field experience is a plus but not required.

 - Proven ability to quickly learn complex technical systems (electrical code, hardware, and software tools).

 - 4-year degree or equivalent electrical experience.

 - Strong communication and organization skills – bilingual is a plus but not required.

 - Ability to multitask, remain calm under pressure, de-escalate high pressure situations, be decisive, and practice patience.

 - Desire and ability to think analytically and creatively to resolve complex issues and suggest process improvements.

 - Attention to detail in communicating accurately and clearly, tracking field interactions, and documenting solutions.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast-paced environment to quickly adapt to changes while maintaining high-quality support.

 - Tech savvy, with a knack for quickly mastering new tools and systems.

 - Team player motivated by the mission who always puts the company’s best interests first.



About the Team

Deployment Engineering is Base Power’s mission control for field operations, acting as the real-time support system for our installation crews. This team sits at the intersection of field electricians, engineering, and member experience, ensuring every install and service call runs smoothly, safely, and efficiently.

Beyond live troubleshooting, the team plays a key role in identifying trends, improving deployment playbooks, and influencing product and operational decisions. Their work directly impacts installation speed, system uptime, and the overall member experience—making them a critical driver of our growth.

This is a team built for people who enjoy fast-paced problem solving, cross-functional collaboration, and developing a full-stack understanding of hardware, software, and field operations.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

title: Senior Accounting Manager
description:
ABOUT BROCCOLI AI

At Broccoli, we're building AI teammates for the people who build and maintain our world.

We partner with plumbing, HVAC, and electrical contractors, the hardworking businesses that keep homes and communities running, and replace fragmented software and repetitive manual work with AI that actually gets the job done.

Our AI teammates answer phones, book appointments, follow up with customers, recover missed revenue, and help contractors deliver exceptional customer experiences, all while integrating seamlessly with platforms like ServiceTitan.

Before we wrote a single line of code, we visited more than 140 contractors to understand how these businesses truly operate. That firsthand experience shaped everything we've built.

Today:

 - Hundreds of contractors rely on Broccoli every day.

 - We've grown to $25M+ ARR in under two years.

 - We're trusted by everyone from independent contractors to some of the largest private equity backed operators in the home services industry.

 - We're backed by Khosla Ventures and Y Combinator.

We're still just getting started.



THE ROLE

We're hiring a Senior Accounting Manager, our first in-house accountant, to own Broccoli's accounting, payroll, and tax end to end. You'll run the close, own revenue accounting for a fast-growing, usage-based business, keep us compliant in every state we operate in, and build the controls and systems that get us audit ready.

This is a deeply hands-on role reporting to our Head of Finance. You'll do the work yourself, make the accounting calls and document them, and work with our external accountant and outside tax advisors. You'll partner with Sales, Customer Success, People and Engineering. There's real building to do: a faster close, cleaner revenue data, tighter controls, and an AI-native finance stack where automation carries the repetitive work.



WHERE WE ARE TODAY

We run on QuickBooks Online, with Measure on top of Stripe for billing, Rippling for payroll and HR, and Brex for cards, bill pay and reimbursements. Revenue mixes subscription fees with usage-based billing, across customers from single-location contractors to multi-site enterprise operators. We have a US company and a subsidiary in India, and an external accountant who handles day-to-day transactions today and will work with you.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the close and the financial statements. Run the close calendar, journal entries, accruals and reconciliations across bank, card, Stripe and payroll. Deliver accurate monthly financials and flux analysis on a business-day-10 timeline, then make it faster.

 - Own revenue accounting and billing. Set and document our ASC 606 policies for subscription, usage-based and multi-location enterprise contracts. Own the billing system (Measure, on Stripe), its sync to the GL, usage accruals and true-ups, and invoice adjustments.

 - Own AR and AP. Run collections, reserves and write-off policy across a customer base that runs from single-location contractors to large multi-site operators. Own vendor setup, bank-detail verification, bill pay, and card and reimbursement policy in Brex against a defined approval matrix, with real segregation of duties.

 - Own payroll. Run payroll in Rippling end to end, including new hires, terminations, pay changes, benefits deductions and off-cycle payments, and reconcile every run to the GL. Own multi-state payroll tax: registrations as we hire in new states, withholding, unemployment insurance, filings, and year-end W-2s and 1099s.

 - Own tax. Stand up sales tax: run the nexus analysis, register where we need to, then set up and enable tax calculation in our billing system and own the filings. Manage income and franchise tax with our outside advisors, plus 1099s and state annual filings.

 - Run treasury operations. Execute bank and card operations, wires and cash movements within approved limits, and keep cash reconciled across our accounts.

 - Get us audit ready. Build the policies, controls and schedules (revenue, equity compensation under ASC 718, prepaids and accruals) that make a first audit and investor diligence straightforward.

 - Support planning and reporting. Deliver clean, on-time actuals for budgeting and for board and investor reporting.

 - Run the international side. Own accounting, statutory compliance and intercompany funding for our India subsidiary, working with local providers.

 - Automate the work. Help choose and implement our next-generation GL, and build the automation that lets a small team run a growing company's books, so AI does the work rather than just reporting on it.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7–10 years of accounting experience, including time in-house at a venture-backed startup.

 - CPA license.

 - Big 4 or comparable public accounting experience, ideally with technology clients.

 - You've owned a monthly close and the financial statements end to end, and you've made and documented the accounting calls behind them.

 - Strong command of US GAAP, including ASC 606.

 - You've run payroll yourself, or you're ready to own it hands-on from day one.

 - You like doing the work. You're as comfortable fixing a reconciliation yourself as designing the process that prevents the next one.

 - You use AI tools in your accounting work today and have a view on where they help.

 - Excellent written communication, with the judgment to explain an accounting call to non-finance partners and to know which calls need escalating.

 - Excited to work in person five days a week with the team in San Francisco.

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field.



BONUS POINTS

 - Usage-based or hybrid SaaS revenue under ASC 606.

 - You've run payroll in Rippling, including multi-state employees and off-cycle payments.

 - QuickBooks Online, Brex, and a subscription billing platform (Measure, Maxio, Chargebee, Stripe Billing or similar), including getting its data to tie to the GL.

 - You've taken a company through its first financial statement audit or a fundraising diligence process.

 - You've set up sales tax or multi-state payroll tax compliance from scratch.

 - You've migrated a company onto an AI-native accounting platform (Rillet, Campfire or similar).

 - Multi-entity or international subsidiary accounting, ideally India.

 - Commission accounting (ASC 340-40) or sales comp administration.

 - SQL or comfort pulling your own data.

 - Experience in home services or B2B SaaS selling to SMBs.



THIS ROLE MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU IF

 - You want to build and manage a team in your first year. You may be our only in-house accountant for a while.

 - You'd rather review work than do it.

 - You're looking for a remote or hybrid role.

location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY; Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Denver, CO; Washington, DC; Austin, TX; Phoenix, AZ; Los Angeles, CA; Seattle, WA; Boston, MA; United States- Remote
description:
About the Team
Our sales and success teams are the heart and soul of DoorDash, helping us partner with top merchants (think restaurants, grocers, convenience stores, retailers) across the country to grow their revenue and help them operate even better. As DoorDash grows both in scale and scope of offering, the strength of our sales engine and organizational structure must grow with it.
About the role
We are looking for a Manager in Sales Strategy and Operations to be the strategic and operational partner to our SMB Business Development (BD) team as it expands its remit and increases restaurant coverage. You will own the operating foundation for BD’s merchant sales motion, including goal setting, pipeline management, lead allocation, and performance reporting.
In this role, you will make sure we are  Making efficient, data-driven decisions,
Building scalable operating systems for a growing sales motion,
Using and advocating for AI tooling, and
Centralizing the metrics that drive sales performance. You’ll work with our Sales, Selection, Operations, Product, Finance, and Analytics teams to build and scale that foundation, helping BD win new restaurant partners and grow those partnerships.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Build from first principles. BD's sales motion is evolving to capture top restaurants in priority markets, and this role will design how it runs: goal structures, input and activity metrics, pipeline stages, and rules of engagement with adjacent sales teams. You'll question "this is how it's always been done" and build what the team needs next.
Drive operational excellence. You'll set up and run reporting cadences, rigorous pipeline reviews, and productivity inspection with sales leaders, taking each one end to end from idea to execution and grounding decisions in data.
Own lead strategy and GTM targeting. You’ll partner with our GM teams to point BD reps at the highest-value opportunities, with clear ownership across teams.
Operate at 10,000 feet and 1 foot. One day you'll size goals and model capacity for a growing team. The next you'll be in diagnosing and improving data fidelity or tracing a pacing gap to its root cause.
Look around corners with AI. You'll find where AI tooling can remove manual work from sales operations and reporting, then build and scale those solutions, helping the team become more efficient as it grows.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 6+ years of experience in sales strategy and operations, revenue operations, consulting, business development, analytics, or related fields, with a track record of leading initiatives and hitting goals
You have experience standing up or scaling sales operating systems, such as goaling and compensation inputs, pipeline management, territory or lead allocation, and CRM workflows (Salesforce or similar)
You are highly proficient in SQL and comfortable working independently with large, complex data sets, and you are skilled at modeling in Excel / Google Sheets and building dashboards in visualization tools (e.g. Sigma, Tableau)
You are fluent with AI tools (e.g. LLMs, AI-assisted coding and automation) and have used them to automate workflows, speed up analysis, or improve data quality, with the judgment to validate outputs carefully
You are a strong business thinker who lets data win arguments and can tell a clear story behind the numbers to audiences from frontline managers to senior leaders
You have strong cross-functional, project management, and communication skills, and you can align multiple stakeholders around a shared plan
You are an owner with a strong bias for action, comfortable with ambiguity, and willing to roll up your sleeves and flex up or down as needed
You have a Bachelor's degree or higher
Why You'll Love Working at DoorDash…
We are leaders – Leadership is not limited to our management team. It's something everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies.
We are operators – We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions to lead our company and our industry is what we do on every project, every day.
We are learners – Everyone here is continually learning on the job, no matter if we've been in a role for one year or one minute. We are committed to learning and implementing what is best for our customers, merchants, and dashers.
We are one team – The magic of DoorDash is our people, together making our inspiring goals attainable and driving us to greater heights.

title: Principal Visual Designer, Merchant
location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY; Seattle, WA
description:
About the Team
At DoorDash, design means making experiences for the people who order, the people who prepare, and the people who deliver. As a Designer at DoorDash, you want to build things that matter to real people. You're at your best when you can move from idea to shipped product quickly, bringing experiences to life that reach and influence users at massive scale. You'll care about whether the product you make solved a real problem for real people, or changed how someone experiences their day.
You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering and Product Management, dig into the data, and use LLM-powered tools alongside traditional design tools. If the LLM powered tools don’t exist yet, you build them.
About the Role
Restaurants are the heart of every neighborhood, yet most run on a patchwork of disconnected tools. We’re building DashOS, the operating system for the restaurant of the future. It’s one platform that connects delivery, in-store dining, reservations, and loyalty, across software, kiosk and POS hardware, and agentic experiences that take work off operators’ plates.
As Principal Visual Designer, you’ll set the look, feel, and identity of DoorDash’s merchant products. You’ll own the visual direction for DashOS and give merchants a recognizable identity across every surface, including hardware, where no design conventions exist yet. These products already work. Your job is to make merchants love using them.
Visual craft is the center of this role, and you’ll ship it yourself. You’ll prototype and use AI tools like Cursor and Claude to generate and refine UI, so your ideas reach production with full fidelity. You’ll also define the visual foundation of the design system (tokens, components, guidance, and examples) so designers, engineers, and AI tools all produce on-brand, high-quality UI. Engineering partners build and maintain the tooling, and you set the rules and the quality bar.
You’ll report to the Senior Director, Product Design for Merchant. This role is hybrid, with 1–2 days a week in a Design Hub.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Set the visual direction for merchant products across DashOS and bring multiple teams around a shared vision, so the work compounds instead of duplicating.
Ship high-craft interfaces with a clear point of view , turning complex, data-dense workflows into screens merchants can read at a glance in a busy kitchen or at the counter.
Own the visual foundation of the design system : define the tokens, components, usage rules and examples that both people and AI tools apply. Review generated UI against that bar, record what good looks like, and improve the system based on how teams actually use it.
Design for new surfaces. Create visual systems for points-of-sale, handhelds and agentic experiences where no existing paradigm applies.
Influence through the work. Earn trust with prototypes and shipped products instead of decks, and keep your prototypes production-ready.
Raise the bar across the team. Mentor senior designers, help close strong hires, and help people sharpen their sense of what to build and why.
We’re excited about you because…
You’ve designed interfaces that defined or reshaped a product’s look and feel, and your portfolio shows top-of-bar visual craft with range across brands and styles.
You can build what you design. You work in React, TypeScript or similar, and use AI tools to explore directions and refine UI faster than you could by hand.
You’ve set direction across a product area, and people adopted your work because it was good, not because you told them to.
You’d rather build a visual system that makes 20 designers faster and more consistent than ship one great screen yourself.
You’ve worked on complex, information-dense products such as point-of-sale, fintech, marketplaces or platform teams, and you’ve shipped with product and engineering partners, including pushing back constructively.
Bonus: you’ve designed for devices or contexts with no existing design paradigm and built the visual system from scratch.

title: Senior Software Engineer, ML Serving Platform
location: San Francisco, CA; Sunnyvale, CA; Seattle, WA
description:
About the Team
DoorDash’s ML Serving Platform delivers tens of millions of predictions per second across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, powering search, recommendations, advertising, and logistics. We build request routing, online feature retrieval, and CPU/GPU inference capabilities that help ML and product teams deploy and operate models independently.
About the Role
We’re looking for a hands-on senior engineer to lead core serving investments. We’re especially interested in engineers who have scaled ranking and recommendation systems in production. You’ll make architectural decisions, write production code, and guide delivery with ML, product, and compute infrastructure partners.
Your first 6–12 months will focus on enabling new ranking and recommendation models, including generative approaches, in online production. You’ll resolve bottlenecks with early product partners and turn those solutions into reusable platform capabilities. Success means faster adoption while meeting model quality, latency, reliability, and cost targets.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead projects from customer problem through design, implementation, and rollout. Coordinate delivery across engineers, mentor peers, and help shape the team’s roadmap.
Improve inference performance through production traces, load tests, and CPU/GPU profiling. Work with model owners to balance model quality, tail latency, throughput, and cost.
Partner with Compute on capacity, placement, and scaling, accounting for request complexity, cache state, GPU memory, and model startup behavior.
Build self-serve APIs and deployment workflows that manage models, runtime dependencies, features, and versioned state, with validation, safe rollout, and rollback.
Evaluate, integrate, and extend open source tools and vendor capabilities that advance model serving. Decide when to build or adopt, and collaborate with maintainers and vendors.
Own production reliability through service objectives, observability, on-call, incident response, and follow-through. Reduce recurring operational work through automation.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 6+ years of software engineering experience designing, building, and operating production infrastructure or distributed systems.
You have hands-on experience serving large or complex neural models online, with accountability for latency, availability, and resource efficiency.
You bring strong distributed systems fundamentals and proficiency in a backend or systems language such as Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, or C++.
You understand inference tradeoffs across batching, concurrency, caching, memory, and CPU/GPU utilization, and can diagnose production bottlenecks.
You have operated services on Kubernetes or comparable infrastructure, including resource configuration, autoscaling, and failure recovery.
You’ve led substantial projects through ambiguity, partnered with fast-moving ML or product teams, and helped other engineers grow.
You hold a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or have equivalent practical experience.
Nice to Have
Experience integrating or extending inference tools such as Triton Inference Server or PyTorch.
Experience with multi-GPU inference, model parallelism, model-aware caching, or accelerator scheduling.
Experience building model workflows, deployment tooling, or instrumentation with Metaflow, Helm, or OpenTelemetry.
We value production serving depth and engineering judgment; experience with every technology is not required.

title: Team Lead, Critical Investigations
description:
About the Team
DoorDash's Critical Investigations Team plays a critical role in ensuring the safety of our platform and the communities we serve. The team is responsible for investigating internal fraud cases to protect company assets and maintain the integrity of our operations. CIU operates in high-stakes, time-sensitive situations, requiring precision, discretion, and a deep understanding of legal and regulatory frameworks.
About the Role
The Critical Investigations Unit (CIU) Team Lead is a key position responsible for overseeing high-impact investigations and guiding specialized teams including our Law Enforcement Response Team. This role addresses the most sensitive, time-critical, and complex cases within the Trust & Safety organization. The ideal candidate will be an experienced investigator with extensive knowledge of law enforcement response, fraud detection, and critical incident triage. The CIU Team Lead will report directly to the CIU Supervisor.

We are seeking a full-time Program Manager for Customer Support Strategy, based on-site at our DFW1 facility in Lewisville, TX. Your focus is reducing ticket volume, claims, and contra revenue, and improving the merchant experience. AI strategy and Zendesk optimization are key levers along the way.

Program Ownership and Strategy:
Own omnichannel customer support programs from inception to execution, aligned to business goals and merchant needs.
Develop strategies with cross-functional teams, incorporating stakeholder feedback and industry best practices.

Ticket Reduction:
Analyze ticket data to find the top contact drivers, size them by volume, handle time, and cost, and build a prioritized reduction roadmap with clear targets.
Support processes: redesign workflows, macros, routing, and agent guidance so issues are resolved faster with fewer repeat contacts.
Ops processes: work with operations and site teams to fix the upstream breakdowns that create tickets, such as inbound, inventory, order, and billing issues.

Evaluate vendors and models, run pilots with clear success criteria, and take proven use cases into production.

description:

Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Exciting Trade Advisory Opportunity to Help Make Global Trade Easy
The Opportunity:
The global supply chain is one of the most heavily regulated industries for all parties involved.  Everyone from the carriers, intermediaries, trucking companies, 3rd party logistics, freight forwarders, shippers, consignees, importers, exporters, and brokers face a challenging and complex task of navigating through a myriad of laws from the originating country, destination country as well as international treaties and conventions.
The Trade Advisory team, consisting of business consultants, lawyers and licensed customs brokers, offers advanced customs and trade expertise to help clients identify supply chain risks and cost savings opportunities. We are looking for a Trade Advisory Associate - Entry Audit to join our Trade Advisory team. This team member will work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to execute client entry audit projects, managing the day-to-day work associated with each engagement from data intake through final reporting and recommendations.
Audit scope: Entry audits review a client's historical import entries to validate compliance and uncover risk and savings opportunities. Scope typically includes tariff classification, customs valuation, country of origin, duty rates and special program eligibility (including free trade agreements and additional tariff programs), antidumping and countervailing duty exposure, and the accuracy of entry data filed in ACE. Findings are quantified, documented, and translated into corrective actions such as prior disclosures, post summary corrections, and duty refund or recovery opportunities.
You Will:
Work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to scope, plan, and execute client entry audit projects.
Manage the day-to-day activities of multiple audit projects, including data requests, timelines, status updates, and deliverables.
Pull, clean, and analyze large volumes of entry-level data from sources such as ACE, client database, entry packets (7501, commercial invoice, packing list, etc.)
Build and maintain Excel models and workbooks to map data from ACE to client specific business rules.
Design, build, and maintain automated workflows and data pipelines using N8N, Parabola, or equivalent tools to streamline audit analysis and reporting.
Identify discrepancies, quantify duty and fee impact, and document audit findings with supporting evidence.
Prepare clear audit reports and client-ready summaries of findings, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Support remediation efforts resulting from audit findings, such as post summary corrections, prior disclosures, and refund or recovery filings.
Maintain internal audit trackers, workpapers, and documentation to ensure projects are organized, consistent, and auditable.
Proactively stay informed on the latest customs and other government agency regulations, ruling issuances, and industry trends that are relevant to our clients.
Ensure project timelines, statuses, and invoices are appropriately managed and delivered.
Identify opportunities to improve audit SOPs, templates, and automation to increase accuracy and efficiency.
Maintain active communication with clients, customs and other government authorities, and internal stakeholders, elevating issues where necessary.
Support Trade Advisory infrastructure and administrative requirements.
You should have:
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university.
Licensed Customs Broker (LCB) preferred.
2-4 years experience working in house, at a customs brokerage, importer, trade industry, preferred.
Strong data analytical skills, with the ability to analyze large data sets and draw accurate conclusions.
Extensive experience with Excel, including advanced formulas, pivot tables, lookups, and large data set analysis.
Experience with workflow automation and data tools such as N8N, python, or equivalent.
Exceptional attention to detail and a high standard of accuracy.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to stay on top of multiple tasks and projects.
Strong technical and business writing skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with a team and with clients.
Expertise with Microsoft Office suite and Google equivalents.
Working knowledge of classification, valuation, country of origin, duty programs, and government regulations and rulings, preferred.

Exciting Trade Advisory Opportunity to Help Make Global Trade Easy
The Opportunity:
The global supply chain is one of the most heavily regulated industries for all parties involved.  Everyone from the carriers, intermediaries, trucking companies, 3rd party logistics, freight forwarders, shippers, consignees, importers, exporters, and brokers face a challenging and complex task of navigating through a myriad of laws from the originating country, destination country as well as international treaties and conventions.
The Trade Advisory team, consisting of business consultants, lawyers and licensed customs brokers, offers advanced customs and trade expertise to help clients identify supply chain risks and cost savings opportunities. We are looking for a Trade Advisory Associate - Entry Audit to join our Trade Advisory team. This team member will work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to execute client entry audit projects, managing the day-to-day work associated with each engagement from data intake through final reporting and recommendations.
Audit scope: Entry audits review a client's historical import entries to validate compliance and uncover risk and savings opportunities. Scope typically includes tariff classification, customs valuation, country of origin, duty rates and special program eligibility (including free trade agreements and additional tariff programs), antidumping and countervailing duty exposure, and the accuracy of entry data filed in ACE. Findings are quantified, documented, and translated into corrective actions such as prior disclosures, post summary corrections, and duty refund or recovery opportunities.

Work closely with the Trade Advisory Lead to scope, plan, and execute client entry audit projects.

Experience with workflow automation and data tools such as N8N, python, or equivalent.

Strong organizational skills and the ability to stay on top of multiple tasks and projects.
Strong technical and business writing skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with a team and with clients.
Expertise with Microsoft Office suite and Google equivalents.
Working knowledge of classification, valuation, country of origin, duty programs, and government regulations and rulings, preferred.

 - Deep understanding of how test parameters interact with electrochemical system performance, and how to separate real signal from test artifacts

Company Overview
Hi-Cone, a division of ITW (NYSE: ITW), is a global leader in sustainable multipackaging solutions for the Alcohol and Non-Alcoholic Ready to Drink (NARTD) beverage markets. We partner with major Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) companies to deliver innovative, environmentally responsible secondary packaging systems. As part of ITW’s decentralized structure, Hi-Cone leverages the ITW Business Model to drive customer-focused innovation, operational excellence, and market leadership.
Position Summary
The Senior Process Engineer serves as the technical leader for extrusion, material conversion, and labeling processes across Hi-Cone's global manufacturing network. This role is responsible for driving process capability, operational excellence, equipment reliability, material utilization, and technology advancement initiatives. Leveraging extensive hands-on manufacturing experience, the Senior Process Engineer develops and implements global manufacturing standards, leads process optimization efforts, supports capital investment projects, and provides technical leadership for strategic initiatives including PCR integration, sustainability objectives, and new product commercialization. The position acts as a subject matter expert for polymer processing, die-cutting/punch press operations, and labeling technologies while partnering with operations, maintenance, quality, and product development teams to improve safety, quality, delivery performance, and cost.

Technology Leadership:
Serve as global Subject Matter Expert (SME) for extrusion, material conversion, and labeling operations.
Establish global process standards, operating windows, control plans, and best practices across all manufacturing facilities.
Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex manufacturing issues impacting safety, quality, throughput, waste, and equipment reliability.
Establish, monitor, and improve process capability metrics and operational benchmarks to drive consistency and performance across global production assets.
