Primary function of Position:
The Director, Learning Technology and Operations is a product-led leader responsible for Intuitive’s enterprise learning technology ecosystem, including SAP SuccessFactors Learning and Percipio. The Director sets the product strategy and roadmap and drives continuous improvement.
This role reports to the Sr. Director, People Tech & Digital Employee Experience. The Director leads and develops the product management and global Learning Management System (LMS) administration teams across the US, India, and Mexico, and builds a scalable support model as the function moves into People Technology. The role partners with IT and Quality Management to keep the platform reliable and compliant, and with Learning & Development, HR, Procurement, and Finance organizations to deliver modern, easy-to-use learning experiences.
The ideal candidate has deep learning platform expertise, experience running learning systems in a regulated environment, and a proven record of leading change. Financial and vendor management skills, and the ability to use AI and automation to improve service and efficiency, round out the profile.
Key Responsibilities
Global Operations & Service Delivery Oversight
Provide leadership oversight for global LMS operations and service delivery across the US, India, and Mexico, working through the Tier 1 and Tier 2 Operations Managers.
Use data, ticket trends, and user feedback to set SLA, quality, and satisfaction targets and to identify where service can be elevated.
Review performance with the Operations Managers on a regular cadence and hold them accountable for results.
Simplify operations by standardizing and automating processes, knowledge content, and reporting, and by removing duplicative work.
Set priorities and guide capacity and investment decisions to balance sustaining support against transformation work as demand grows.
Establish the controls and standards that keep LMS operations accurate, secure, private, and audit-ready, including how approved changes are implemented and how completion records and objective evidence are archived in the GxP system.
Serve as the executive escalation point for critical incidents and for cross-functional and vendor issues.
Leadership & Team Development
Lead the product management team and the global LMS administration team of managers, administrators, and contractors, aligning both to a single product vision and setting clear expectations, goals, and accountability for results.
Develop the team through coaching on complex technology decisions, defined career paths, skills development, and succession planning, building a leadership bench and cross-region capability.
Foster a customer-centric culture focused on learner experience, accountability, continuous improvement, and learning.
Manage workload and priorities across the team and the employee/contractor mix.
Promote agile ways of working and strong cross-functional partnerships across HR, Quality, Technology, and business teams.
Organizational Change & Transition
Lead the planning and execution of the transition of the LMS administration organization, processes, and platform operations into People Technology, with defined milestones, risks, and success measures.
Maintain service continuity, compliance, and audit readiness throughout the transition, with no degradation in SLAs or user experience.
Align operating model, governance, tooling, and ways of working with People Technology and Digital Employee Experience standards, and identify opportunities to share services and capabilities across People Technology platforms.
Lead change management and communication for the team, stakeholders, and users.
Partnership with IT and Quality Management
Partner with IT on the technical roadmap, release schedule, upgrades and patches, integrations, and platform performance, providing clear requirements and acceptance.
Participate in release testing and validation and support IT in creating and maintaining validation documentation.
Establish joint operating rhythms with IT, including release planning, incident and escalation reviews, and shared project tracking, so that service issues and platform changes are resolved quickly.
Partner with Quality Management so that approved training content, assignments, and removals are implemented accurately and on time.
Support quality audits and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) by providing LMS reports and records when requested.
Align LMS processes and work instructions with quality procedures and change control and establish clear decision rights and escalation paths with IT, Quality, and Learning & Development.
Financial Accountability
Own the annual budget for the learning technology operations, vendor services, contractors, and program spend; forecast accurately and manage variances.
Build business cases and ROI/TCO analyses for new capabilities, platform changes, and resourcing decisions, and present them to senior leadership.
Drive efficiencies and cost avoidance through license and content rationalization, process standardization, and optimization of the regional and employee/contractor delivery mix.
Track and report operating metrics such as cost per ticket, cost per learner, and license utilization to demonstrate value and guide investment decisions.
Vendor Management
Act as the key liaison between internal customers, technical resources, and vendors, and jointly own with IT the relationships and contracts with SAP, Percipio, learning content providers, and managed service and contractor partners, including negotiation, renewals, and commercial terms in partnership with Procurement.
Hold vendors accountable to SLAs, quality standards, and roadmap commitments through regular performance reviews, and escalate and resolve issues.
Drive key product enhancements on behalf of Intuitive and represent Intuitive’s needs in vendor roadmaps and user communities.
Product Management & Strategy
Own the product vision and roadmap for the learning technology ecosystem, and align it with IT’s technical roadmap, in sync with Intuitive’s business growth goals and people priorities.
Translate business needs, voice-of-customer input, and enhancement requests into a prioritized, scalable roadmap with clear KPIs and measurable outcomes.
Define release requirements, confirm acceptance of scope and lock scope with IT, and establish and execute the global launch plan, including training, collateral, and communications.
Define and execute LMS controls, permissions, and best practices, and own monitoring of all learning domains.
Establish an operating model for the large community of stakeholders and departments that request and maintain learning content, including intake, standards, and lifecycle management, in partnership with Learning & Development.
Governance, Quality & Compliance
Govern policy and practice through cross-functional learning technology governance forums, including executive and advisory input.
Ensure LMS operations meet audit readiness, certification governance, and GxP-compliant record-keeping requirements defined by Quality and Regulatory, working with IT on the validated state of the platform.
Own release documentation, including work instructions and procedures, and oversee the functional health of integrations with systems such as Veeva, Workday, product lifecycle management, and ServiceNow.
Learning Experience & Skills-Based Enablement
Lead the evolution of how employees discover, access, and engage with learning through improved search, personalization, guided workflows, and self-service.
Define the functional requirements and data model needs to support skills-based talent development in partnership with Talent Management, Learning & Development, and HR systems teams.
AI & Automation
Evaluate and adopt AI and automation capabilities available in SAP SuccessFactors, Percipio, and ServiceNow, such as intelligent support and case deflection and administrative automation, piloting and scaling high-value use cases that improve service quality and efficiency.
Ensure AI and automation solutions align with governance, compliance, data security, privacy, and responsible AI standards, including validation expectations in a regulated environment.
Analytics, Adoption & Continuous Improvement
Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including SLA attainment, user satisfaction, self-service adoption, content quality, cost efficiency, and program outcomes.
Communicate progress, outcomes, and business value to HR and executive leadership.
Skills, Experience, Education & Training
Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum 12+ years of learning technology or HR technology experience with proven results in creating technical strategies, developing business requirements, deploying technologies, and business process re-engineering.
Minimum 7+ years leading, developing, and coaching technical or operational teams.
Minimum bachelor’s degree in technology, business, or a related technical field.
Experience managing learning systems in a regulated environment (medical device, pharmaceutical, or similar), including GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, and quality management system-related training requirements.
Deep expertise in the SAP SuccessFactors Learning platform, including configuration, curriculum and assignment management, integrations, release management, and administration at enterprise scale.
Experience leading global, multi-tier support operations with defined SLAs and ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow), including teams that combine employees and contractors, at a company with employee populations across multiple regions.
Experience partnering with IT and Quality organizations on validated system releases, change control, and audit support.
Experience owning a budget and managing vendor relationships and contracts, with a track record of driving cost efficiencies.
Demonstrated product management experience, including owning a roadmap, prioritizing against competing demands, and measuring outcomes with KPIs.
Strong customer orientation and superb communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical, functional, and executive audiences; strong personal and technical influencing skills.
Strong collaborator who can engage and influence partners across the company and define clear ownership and decision rights with peer functions; interacts frequently with internal and external senior-level leadership.

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The People Analytics Analyst owns end to end analytics products from data source to analytical products (Apps/Dashboards/reports). The role is the subject matter expert for HCM data and reporting. It turns data from the applicant tracking system (ATS), Workday, Anaplan, Qualtrics and other HR systems into trusted, easy-to-use insights that help HR and business leaders make better decisions. The analyst works independently with little day-to-day instruction, resolves moderate to complex problems, and supports less experienced colleagues.
Roles and Responsibilities
Analytics products and dashboards
Design, build and maintain apps, dashboards and reports in
Partner with other organizations such HR Operations, People Services, TA leadership, HR Business Partner (HRBP) leaders and Finance in a consultative role to understand business questions, scope requirements, and recommend the right metrics, methods and analyses.
Identify, analyze and interpret trends to support workforce and talent decisions, and recommend process improvements based on data patterns such as bottlenecks and conversion rates.
Translate findings into clear, visually effective stories and present or demo them to HR, TA and business leadership.
Develop templates and automation, including AI-assisted tools, for recurring requests so that common reporting is standardized and low effort to maintain.
Data management, integration and governance
Query, model and combine data from disparate sources (Workday, ATS, Anaplan, Qualtrics, Snowflake and the enterprise data warehouse) to deliver regular and ad hoc reporting.
Work with HRIS, IT and the Enterprise Analytics team to design and support integrations and data models, and to identify opportunities to improve data management.
Define and document standard metric and data definitions, and run recurring data-quality audits across systems, with remediation plans shared with partners.
Monitor dashboard performance and data integrity, test and QA changes, and resolve issues quickly.
Take part in the development and implementation of data governance, partnering with key stakeholders.
Collaboration and growth
Manage projects and priorities across multiple stakeholders, adjusting as business needs change.
Coach and support less experienced team members and partners in using data and tools effectively.
Apply sound statistical understanding so that insights are accurate, and pilot predictive approaches where they add value.
Keep learning new tools and methods, including AI and advanced analytics, and bring improvements to the team.
Skills and Job Requirements
Required
Bachelor’s degree with 5 years of related experience in data analytics and visualization, business intelligence or analytical consulting; or a Master’s degree with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience.
Proven ability to use data, analytics and business knowledge to solve moderate to complex business problems.
Hands-on experience with Tableau (or an equivalent data visualization tool), strong SQL skills against a relational database and AI integrated workflows (Ex. Claude/Devin/Cortex -> Git -> Products).
Experience combining data from multiple systems into reliable reporting, with attention to data quality.
Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to simplify complex information for different audiences and to influence stakeholders.
Experience getting to a first working version, gathering real-world feedback, and iterating, with a continuous improvement mindset.
HR or talent analytics experience, and familiarity with Workday (reporting, Prism or integrations) and ATS data.
Preferred
Master’s degree.
Experience with Snowflake or a cloud data warehouse.
R or Python.
Experience with project management tools and with AI or automation tools applied to analytics.
Level Expectations (Professional 3)
Scope: A seasoned professional with a full understanding of the area of specialization; resolves a wide range of issues in creative ways.
Complexity: Works on problems of diverse scope; demonstrates good judgment in selecting methods and techniques; networks with senior internal and external personnel in own area of expertise.
Communication: Builds important internal and external relationships through advanced communication skills; influences and negotiates effectively.
Supervision: Receives little instruction on day-to-day work and general instructions on new assignments; occasional management direction and review of activities and priorities.
Decision making: Independently resolves moderate to more complex problems; supports less experienced team members in making effective decisions.

The purpose of this role is to serve as a Scientific Research Program Manager (SRPM) supporting evidence strategy and research programs across Intuitive Surgical’s da Vinci platforms, products, and services. The SRPM will collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to identify evidence needs and priorities and support the development and execution of evidence-generation strategies and research plans. This role oversees the initiation, progress, and conduct of evidence-generation studies, including those conducted by internal scientific teams, Intuitive-sponsored studies, and studies conducted in collaboration with external research partners. The SRPM serves as a key contact for internal and external parties involved in assigned programs and projects.
Essential Job Duties
Collaborate with da Vinci and Multiport program leaders and cross-functional evidence stakeholders to identify evidence requirements and gaps, align on evidence priorities, and develop evidence strategies and plans.
Manage and execute a portfolio of internal and external collaborative research studies and evidence-generation activities for Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci platforms, products, and services, with support from research coordinators as applicable.
Manage research studies across the study lifecycle, including project development, budgeting, investigator selection, analysis of potential participant recruitment, preparation of study-related documents (e.g., protocols, case report forms, informed consents, research agreements), and management of Institutional Review Board and/or Ethics Committee submissions through successful outcome.
Collaborate with data management professionals and statisticians as needed; maintain required study documentation; and plan and manage project timelines and budgets to support timely execution.
Proactively identify and communicate project concerns, issues, and delays; develop risk assessments and contingency plans; and prepare project status updates, presentations, and reports for internal and external stakeholders and steering or advisory committees.
Manage publication development, submission, and responses to peer review related to research studies.
Ensure compliance with corporate requirements (e.g., SOPs) and applicable regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and U.S. and international guidelines), and maintain audit readiness to relevant regulatory and legal standards.
Manage Contract Research Organizations (CROs) and independent research service providers, including partner identification, contract or statement-of-work development, and stakeholder management; facilitate meetings and reporting in accordance with Intuitive Surgical policies; and support review and development of internal research processes (e.g., SOPs).
Build, nurture, and maintain relationships with external research partners and stakeholders, including surgeon key opinion leaders, operating room staff, hospital and health system administrative and technology leaders, surgical and scientific professional society leaders, and healthcare technology industry partners.
Skills, Experience, Education, & Training:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field
Minimum five years of experience in an academic setting or healthcare technology industry in a clinical affairs or scientific research function, with evidece of full project management responsibility; industry research management experience preferred.
Knowledge of applicable clinical research and medical device regulations and guidelines, including GCP, ISO 14155, MEDDEV, MDR, and data protection requirements.
Experience developing research protocols and case report forms (CRFs).
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects with competing priorities, including a minimum of three to five research projects across different surgical disciplines and/or products.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills, with the ability to manage work autonomously and collaborate across teams while maintaining open communication with key stakeholders.
Strong quantitative and literature analysis skills, with the ability to assess data and scientific literature and review data sets for data quality.
Ability to manage CROs, external consultants, research coordinators, or other research staff in the execution of research studies.
Strong problem-solving skills and initiative; English-language proficiency required.
English language required, a second language is an advantage
Work may require presence in hospital and surgical/operating room environments. Ability to travel 25%-50% of the time.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Graduate degree in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field.
Five years of experience in the management of research, including clinical research management experience in both academic/hospital and industry settings.
Experience with studies of health information technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Experience publishing research in an academic or industry capacity.
Proficiency in a second language.

Primary Function of Position
We are seeking an experienced Senior BI Analyst to support the design and delivery of Finance reporting, analytics, data products, and process-improvement solutions. Working closely with the Finance Product Owner, this role will serve as an onsite analytical partner to Finance stakeholders and a key link between business, application, data engineering, and reporting teams.
The ideal candidate combines Finance and ERP process knowledge with strong SQL, data analysis, and business intelligence capabilities. Operating at the intersection of business logic and data engineering, you will understand complex business processes, trace data lineage across systems, investigate discrepancies, and translate business needs into clear reporting models and technical requirements. You will design and deliver trusted dashboards, BI data models, operational monitoring, and self-service analytics while evaluating practical automation and AI-assisted analytics opportunities (deep AI/ML engineering experience is not required).
Essential Job Duties
Technical Translation & Requirements Gathering: Partner with the Finance Product Owner and Finance stakeholders to understand business processes, controls, and reporting needs. Translate business needs into functional and data requirements, business rules, report specifications, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
BI Design & Solution Delivery: Design, build, and maintain Finance dashboards, published data sources, BI data models, operational reports, and self-service analytics solutions using Tableau, Power BI, or comparable platforms.
Lineage, Reconciliation & Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze end-to-end processes and data flows across ERP (SAP), CRM, billing, data warehouse, and reporting platforms. Use advanced SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data, validate business rules, investigate discrepancies, and identify root causes.
Performance Tuning & Reporting Reliability: Optimize dashboard usability, query performance, data refresh schedules, metric consistency, and overall reporting reliability.
Delivery Leadership & Governance : Lead assigned workstreams through requirements, solution design, UAT, regression testing, reconciliation, implementation readiness, and stakeholder sign-off. Maintain data definitions, reporting specifications, test evidence, user guides, and governance documentation.
Internal Controls & Quality Monitoring: Support automated monitoring, exception management, data-quality controls, and financially significant/SOX-governed reporting processes.
Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration: Collaborate with application, Data Engineering, Data Science, AI, and platform teams while coordinating and reviewing deliverables across distributed onsite and offshore resources.
Applied AI & Automation Evaluation: Evaluate and support opportunities to implement intelligent alerts, natural-language analytics, AI-assisted analysis, and workflow automation within core Finance processes.
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
7+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, Finance analytics, reporting, business systems analysis, or enterprise data solutions.
ERP & Finance Domain: Experience with SAP or another enterprise ERP platform, including strong understanding of Finance-related processes and cross-system data flows.
Advanced SQL Mastery: Expert-level SQL skills for complex querying, source-to-target reconciliation, data troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and query performance optimization.
Enterprise BI Platforms: Strong hands-on experience designing dashboards, BI data models, calculated metrics, published data sources, and self-service solutions in Tableau , Power BI , or a comparable enterprise analytics platform.
Data Architecture Fundamentals: Solid understanding of data warehousing concepts, dimensional modeling, semantic layers, data quality, lineage, and visualization best practices.
Delivery & Testing Leadership: Demonstrated experience translating business needs into technical specifications and leading UAT, regression testing, issue resolution, and business-readiness activities.
Communication & Influence: Proven ability to communicate complex business, system, and data topics to technical teams, Finance stakeholders, and senior leadership without direct authority.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with SAP Finance, Salesforce, CPQ/CLM, billing, or revenue-management platforms.
Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data platform.
Experience supporting financially significant applications, internal controls, or SOX-governed reporting.
Familiarity with data governance, master data management (MDM), metadata, lineage, and data-quality frameworks.
Exposure to AI-assisted analytics, natural-language querying, intelligent monitoring, Snowflake Cortex, or comparable emerging technologies.
Experience coordinating and reviewing work with distributed onsite and offshore analysts or consultants.
Required Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Systems, Business Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field.
What Success Looks Like
Develops a strong understanding of Finance processes, ERP applications, system integrations, critical data models, and reporting dependencies.
Establishes effective translation and validation practices between Finance stakeholders and technical delivery teams, serving as a trusted onsite partner.
Delivers accurate, intuitive, and performant dashboards and BI solutions that stakeholders trust for day-to-day decision-making and operational reviews.
Independently uses SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data across systems, trace transformations, validate business rules, and identify root causes.
Improves reporting reliability and governance , expanding exception monitoring, data-quality controls, metric consistency, and self-service analytics adoption.
Helps Finance teams adopt automation and AI-assisted analytics where they provide measurable business value and practical process improvements.

Train technicians and manufacturing staff in new processes and quality standards.

Willingness to travel occasionally to suppliers or manufacturing sites

BS in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or related field

Experience in medical device manufacturing (ISO 13485)
Familiarity with ISO 9001 and regulated product development environments
Hands-on experience with catheter, needle, or minimally invasive device assemblies, including packaging and sterilization validation
Experience with Agile and SAP systems or equivalent
Demonstrated success in experimental design and structured problem solving
Experience in Controlled Environment Rooms (CER)

Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.

Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.

Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback  and experiences  to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.

Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Demonstrates advanced proficiency and autonomy within established procedures and practices. Frequently consulted by peers. May act as lead coordinating the work of others.

Leadership: Typically has no supervisory or Line Manager responsibilities. May act as informal resource for others. Can be a team leader; allocates work coordinating activities, checking on quality and work progress.

Equipment maintenance and troubleshooting

Reliability and continuous improvement initiatives

Technical leadership, training, and mentoring

Overview
As a  Critical Environment Technician (CET)  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Surface unknown threats

Enforcement policies

description:
Overview
The Frontier Transformation Framework helps our customers become Frontier Firms: organizations where AI is not a tool added to the business but part of the operating system the business runs on. The single biggest reason AI programs stall is not the technology; 95% of AI pilots fail to deliver meaningful P&L impact because they are deployed without a value hypothesis, measure the wrong things, or never baseline before building. Value Creation and Management is the discipline that closes that gap, turning AI from a cost center with unclear returns into a tracked investment with board-level visibility. The Frontier Transformation team is how the Microsoft Frontier Company, the organization this role sits within, delivers this: a small, human-agent team in which each member carries one of the Framework's eight capabilities into the customer, directs a set of digital co-workers to deliver at a scale headcount alone could not, and is designed to fade into a customer counterpart who can carry the work forward.
We are seeking a Principal Value Creation Lead  to define, design, and prove the business value of AI and agentic investment across strategic customer engagements. In this role, you will own the Value Realization Framework end to end: surfacing where AI investment aligns with a customer's strategic objectives, building the value hypotheses and investment cases that unlock funding, declaring the measurement approach before anything is built, and proving realized outcomes against baselines once solutions are live. You will operate at the intersection of finance, business strategy, engineering, and field delivery, working directly with CFOs, executive sponsors, account teams, Industry Business Architects, and delivery pods.
This is a role for people who are equally comfortable in a CFO-led value workshop and in the detail of a P&L model, who can move from strategic ambition to a defensible financial figure, and who are energized by making value real rather than anecdotal. You will help customers see, fund, and capture the value of becoming a Frontier Firm, while shaping the reusable value patterns, benchmarks, and playbooks that scale this discipline across industries. If you are excited by the opportunity to make AI investment measurable, fundable, and provable, this role is for you.
Responsibilities
Lead value discovery through the Value Realization Framework, running facilitated (often CFO-led) workshops that identify where AI and agent investment aligns with the customer's strategic business objectives.
Build and own value hypotheses for each candidate use case, framed as a single testable statement and mapped to the four value themes: Enrich Employee Experience, Reinvent Customer Experience, Reshape Business Processes, and Bend the Innovation Curve.
Produce value-ranked agent backlogs, prioritizing opportunities by business value, feasibility, and time-to-impact using the Value Rubric and Frontier Guide (Today-vs-Frontier benchmarks).
Develop the Business Case that unlocks funding: a three-scenario financial model (Conservative, Expected, Optimistic) with ROI, time-to-break-even, sensitivity analysis, and an explicit cost of inaction.
Design the Measurement Spine, decomposing the sponsor's Impact KPI into Value Driver KPIs, and defining Adoption Diagnostics (Reach and Depth) that explain why the numbers moved.
Capture before-and-after baselines for every use case ahead of deployment, using quantitative snapshots, user surveys, and stakeholder interviews, so impact can be proven afterward.
Build and run measurement instruments, including the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights and the per-engagement Pulse Dashboard (Power BI) that reads the Measurement Spine live.
Produce the Agentic Business Impact Report, correlating AI and agent deployment to financial KPIs such as cycle time, cost-to-serve reduction, and throughput improvements tied to specific workflows.

The MDASH team is advancing how organizations discover and resolve vulnerabilities in source code. MDASH uses a multi-agent, multi-model system to analyze code, validate whether potential vulnerabilities are real and reachable, and provide developers with concrete fixes and guidance for verifying that code is no longer vulnerable. We are seeking a Principal Security Researcher to build and improve the AI-powered, agentic system at the heart of MDASH vulnerability discovery, validation, and resolution. You will combine deep vulnerability research with AI experimentation: researching vulnerability classes and language ecosystems, identifying representative evaluation targets, building and reviewing ground truth, analyzing missed and incorrect findings, and developing improvements that measurably increase recall, precision, consistency, and fix quality. We are looking for a hands-on vulnerability researcher who can read unfamiliar code, trace attacker-controlled data to security-sensitive operations, develop and use fuzzers and other analysis tools, reproduce vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and reachability, and determine whether a proposed fix addresses the underlying weakness. You will carry research from hypothesis through implementation and measurement, directly building and evaluating improvements to MDASH's agents, tools, model configurations, and analysis methods while collaborating with engineering and applied science partners.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Identify representative evaluation targets and author trusted ground truth spanning vulnerability evidence, attack paths, severity, validation, and remediation.

About the Team

The AI Deployment team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.

Our mission is to help customers successfully adopt and operationalize AI across their organizations. We partner with enterprises to translate the potential of OpenAI’s technology into durable capability—through structured training, technical enablement, and scalable deployment programs.

By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens product adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.

About the Role

The AI Deployment Manager is a specialist post-sales enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering enablement experiences that support a repeatable adoption framework, driving sustained activation, expanding breadth and depth of usage, and measurable business value across OpenAI’s product suite, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents.

This role blends strong product fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live workshops, deliver services, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from everyday business users to technical practitioners and executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them effectively in real world workflows.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, supporting successful launches of new product capabilities, and helping customers translate product features into tangible outcomes across teams and business functions. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage by shaping how enablement drives measurable customer impact.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across business and technical teams within enterprise organizations.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.

 - Lead customer enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement programs designed for durable, organization-wide adoption.

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solution Architects, and Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.

 - Speak fluent business-level Japanese, as you will be engaging with Japanese-speaking customers

 - Have 6+ years of experience in customer facing, enablement, or instructional roles, engaging C-level, business, and technical audiences in complex enterprise environments.

 - Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when translating AI capabilities into clear, practical value for senior and executive level audiences.

 - Have strong product fluency across ChatGPT, Agents, and the broader OpenAI ecosystem, with a practical understanding of how AI capabilities can be applied to real world workflows and enterprise use cases.

 - Have experience leading workshops and enablement programs, with the ability to design learning journeys, facilitate live sessions, and respond to questions in real time.

 - Can identify patterns across customers and translate them into scalable approaches that improve adoption across the broader customer base.

 - Can connect product capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity gains, operational efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

We are looking for an Audience & Content Growth Lead to build the global content and education programs that inspire, inform and engage SMB advertisers.

You will turn customer needs, product capabilities and advertiser success stories into compelling content—from webinars and educational video series to case studies, industry-specific playbooks and creator-led programs.

The role combines two areas of ownership: developing content specifically for SMB audiences and building effective ways to distribute it. You will lead programs directly while partnering with teams that own web, social, lifecycle marketing, growth and regional channels to reach the right audiences at scale.

 - Set the global SMB content strategy and editorial roadmap, grounded in customer needs, industry priorities, and advertiser maturity.

 - Create compelling customer stories, case studies, vertical playbooks, guides, videos, and thought leadership that make advertising accessible and actionable.

 - Develop creator-, expert-, and customer-led programs that combine credible education, authentic storytelling, and relevant audience reach.

 - Bring 10+ years of experience in content marketing, audience development, or customer education, including programs for SMBs or advertisers.

 - Demonstrate ownership of content creation and distribution that grows relevant audiences and drives customer action.

 - Translate complex products into clear, engaging content through strong editorial judgment and storytelling.

 - Build repeatable programs across formats such as webinars, video, customer stories, vertical playbooks, and creator-led content.

 - Lead cross-functional and partner-led distribution, aligning teams around shared priorities and measurable outcomes.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s LATAM Marketing team helps people understand how AI can benefit their lives and put that value into practice. We connect global product innovation with local consumer needs, culture and behavior across Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America, contributing to OpenAI’s mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

We build the ChatGPT brand through integrated campaigns, creator and social programs, partnerships and cultural experiences. We work with local and global teams to make ChatGPT relevant and useful in people’s everyday lives.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on Integrated Marketing Manager to lead Consumer and Brand campaigns across LATAM. The role is based in São Paulo and works closely with regional and global teams.

You’ll turn consumer and cultural insights into a clear brief and a distinctive creative idea that shows why ChatGPT matters in people’s everyday lives. You’ll lead the work from strategy through production and launch, and build ongoing marketing programs that keep the brand relevant from always on to major campaigns.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define the audience, cultural insight, brand objective and role for marketing in each program.

 - Write clear creative briefs, guide concept development and give actionable feedback to internal creative teams and external partners.

 - Own integrated consumer campaigns from brief through launch and measurement. Give paid, owned and earned media, social, creators, partnerships and experiences partners distinct roles in bringing the campaign idea to life.

 - Develop locally originated campaigns and adapt global work for Brazil and other LATAM markets without losing the core brand strategy.

 - Build and run ongoing consumer marketing programs around cultural moments and everyday needs. Set priorities, clarify who owns the work and use each campaign’s learnings to improve the program over time.

 - Align local, regional and global partners on the campaign brief, channel roles and the decisions needed to deliver the work.

title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.



About the Role

We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale.

You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.



We’re looking for someone with:

 - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail.

 - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows.

 - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance.

 - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures.

 - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination.

 - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results.

 - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations.



In this role, you will:

 - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements.

 - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue.

 - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues.

 - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions.

 - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners.

 - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability.

 - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands.

 - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions.

 - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements.

 - Understand how invoices, approvals, supplier records, payment instructions, bank status, settlement, and reconciliation fit together, and can investigate discrepancies across them.

 - Bring a strong controls mindset aligned to SOX, including practical judgment on bank-detail changes, duplicate prevention, segregation of duties, reconciliation, and close support.

 - Have designed or improved ERP/AP payment workflows and bank integrations, including host-to-host automation, with tested controls and measurable results.

 - Have led teams or BPO partners through clear expectations, coaching, capacity planning, and sustained improvements in service and quality.

 - Communicate clearly with suppliers, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and can resolve issues across teams without losing ownership.

 - Are willing to work directly in payment queues, investigate failures, and support close when needed.

 - Experience with Oracle Fusion, Zip, or comparable integrated finance systems, and practical use of AI in controlled finance workflows, would be helpful.

 - Are willing to travel up to 50% and work on-site with national security customers to build strong relationships and deeply understand their needs.

title: Thermal Engineer
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures

 - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials

 - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production

 - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues

 - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs)

 - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management.

 - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency

 - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

 - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools

 - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling

 - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups

 - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling

 - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions

 - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions.

 - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments


PREFERRED SKILLS

 - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware

 - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale

 - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies

 - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques

 - Understanding of reliability testing, failure analysis, and thermal stress testing for electronic components

 - Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing partners to support thermal solution development and production ramp-up

Maintain a clean, safe, and highly organized service center environment, adhering to 5S principles. description:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
Manager, Trial Success
About the Role
Samsara's Trial Success team makes sure enterprise trials are executed with excellence, so prospects see the full value of our solutions and are ready for implementation.
As the Manager, Trial Success, you will lead and develop a team of 6+ Trial Success Managers (TSMs) who run customized trial plans for Enterprise prospects.
You own team results: trial conversion, trial quality, and TSM growth and retention.
You partner with Sales, Sales Engineering, Business Value Strategy, Product, and Customer Success leaders to drive deal progress and a consistent trial experience.
You will also shadow a small number of high-stakes trials yourself, and be able to train new hires & step in as an escalation point for strategic deals.
Remote position, open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
Travel Requirements
Up to 25% travel to Samsara and customer sites in the US and Canada.
Expect 3-5 onsite trips per quarter of 1-2 nights each, including team offsites and 1:1s with TSMs.
Key Responsibilities
People Leadership
Hire and onboard: Build the hiring plan, run structured interviews, make strong hiring decisions, and ramp new TSMs to full productivity with a clear 30/60/90 plan.
Coach continuously: Hold weekly 1:1s, review live trial work and customer calls, and give timely, specific feedback that builds skills in value-based selling, change management, and executive communication.
Manage performance: Set clear goals and expectations, run goal-setting and performance review cycles, and address underperformance early with documented improvement plans when needed.
Develop careers: Create individual development plans, identify stretch assignments, and build a succession pipeline for the next level of TSM and leadership roles.
Calibrate and reward: Participate in calibration, promotion, and compensation cycles with fair, data-backed recommendations.
Build culture and engagement: Foster an inclusive, high-trust team, monitor engagement and burnout, recognize wins, and retain top talent.
Handle people operations: Manage time off, workload balance, coverage plans, and sensitive employee matters in partnership with People/HR.
Team Execution and Operations
Set the team's goals, KPIs, and operating rhythm (pipeline reviews, trial health reviews, weekly close).
Assign TSM coverage by account priority, segment, and capacity, and rebalance as deals shift.
Review trial plans, success criteria, and mutual action plans in Accord to ensure quality and standardization.
Inspect trial health, flag risks early, and lead account team strategy sessions to unblock deals.
Report trial conversion, cycle time, and team health metrics to senior leadership.
Strategy and Cross-Functional Leadership
Own and evolve the trial methodology, including job aids, communication templates, and playbooks.
Partner with Sales, SE, BVS, Product, and Support leaders to bring the right resources to the right trial at the right time.
Drive adoption of tools and AI-enabled workflows that increase TSM capacity and trial quality.
Capture customer and field feedback from trials and share it with Product and Enablement.
Represent the team in executive trial reviews and customer-facing escalations.
Champion and model Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team).
What You'll Need to Succeed
Minimum Qualifications
10+ years of experience in a client-facing role working with Enterprise clients (strategic consulting, account management, project management, or sales); SaaS or technology experience preferred.
3+ years of experience directly managing people.
Bachelor's degree required.
Required Skills
Proven ability to hire, coach, develop, and retain high-performing client-facing teams.
Strong project management and change management experience (PMP certification is a plus).
Expertise in communication strategy, risk management, and executive stakeholder management.
Ability to set goals, measure performance with data, and manage by metrics (conversion, cycle time, pipeline).
Experience influencing cross-functional leaders without direct authority.
Exceptional written and verbal communication; able to convey complex ideas concisely.
Strong quantitative and presentation skills.
Technical aptitude with CRM and project management tools.
Comfort in an unstructured, fast-paced, change-heavy environment.
An Ideal Candidate Also Has
Experience managing or scaling a trial, proof-of-concept, or proof-of-value function in software or hardware.
Sales experience closing business with large Enterprise organizations.
Experience supporting large-scale business solutions at Fortune 500 companies.
Experience building team processes, playbooks, and standards from scratch.
A strong bias for action, the ability to think big, and insistence on high standards.

Samsara’s Hardware Reliability team enables an exceptional customer experience by enabling reliable hardware, identifying opportunities in product performance, and engaging cross-functionally to resolve key issues. Samsara’s Senior Hardware Reliability Engineer will design quality processes that guarantee the high-quality standards of Samsara's hardware. In this on-site role, you will also work hands-on in our San Francisco (SF9) labs, running and driving reliability tests with the lab and product design teams.
The Reliability engineer is responsible for implementing and executing comprehensive reliability strategies/plans that span the entire product development lifecycle from concept to warranty repair. The Reliability engineer quickly aggregates and analyzes test, field performance, and manufacturing data to drive actions internally and with our suppliers to ensure that we are building the highest quality product. Cross-functional collaboration with hardware, firmware, and operations is an essential part of the role.
This is an on-site position based in our San Francisco (SF9) office and labs, with regular hands-on work in the lab

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Work cross-functionally with partners in Hardware/Firmware Engineering, Operations, and Support to ensure our customers have a best-in-class product experience.
Design in reliability through the product development process and own product reliability modeling, testing, and validation.
Set reliability requirements and allocate reliability targets to subsystems.
Lead product quality investigations in addition to root cause and corrective actions with internal cross-functional team members and external vendors.
Evaluate and investigate defect trends that improve incoming material and outgoing product quality.
Identify opportunities for corrective actions and continuous improvement through field failure investigations.
Create feedback loops to continuously improve the products in the field and the next generation.
Provide hands-on test execution and lab support at SF9: set up fixtures, run reliability tests (for example thermal, vibration and shock, ingress protection, UV, and chemical or wash exposure), and keep reliability testing on schedule alongside the lab team.
Tailor reliability test plans to each program's risk, working with Product Design, Firmware, Manufacturing, JDM partners, and third-party labs to close findings quickly.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

MS or PhD in Engineering, Material Science, Physics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of experience working in a Hardware Reliability Engineer role.
Hands-on experience planning and executing reliability tests in a lab: stress, fatigue, vibration and shock, thermal cycling, HALT, electrical stress, and environmental stress (including ingress protection, UV, and chemical or wash exposure).
Experience with failure analysis methodologies.
Understanding the physics of failure and the application of stresses to underlying failure mechanisms.
Experience with Design for Reliability concepts.
Experience with JDM development model.
Experience with third-party test oversight, and test execution.
Self-motivated, proactive, creative and critical problem-solving capabilities.
Demonstrated ownership and a hands-on, driver mindset: you run tests yourself, work in the lab, and take issues to closure with minimal direction.
Ability to work through ambiguity and tailor test plans to each program's risk and schedule.
