title: Analyst Relations Senior Manager
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Analyst Relations is a core pillar of Stripe’s enterprise marketing function. The Analyst Relations team creates experiences for the analyst audience that build advocacy and trust, strengthen relationships, and generate insights that inform Stripe's product and go-to-market strategy. Our team crafts high-quality content and builds deep partnerships across product, sales, and marketing to give analysts an accurate, nuanced picture of how Stripe operates and where we're headed. Plus, we bring external perspectives back into the business.
This is an opportunity for a collaborative marketer who excels at translating complex fintech concepts and synthesizing market feedback into accessible insights that sharpen Stripe's strategy.
What you’ll do
You’ll own the global analyst relations strategy and execution for Stripe’s payments, fraud prevention, and agentic commerce portfolio. Reporting to the Head of Analyst Relations, you’ll build trusted analyst relationships, lead evaluations and research engagements, and develop clear, engaging, evidence-backed narratives about Stripe’s products and strategy.
You’ll work cross-functionally to deepen analyst understanding of Stripe and turn analyst feedback into actionable recommendations. The role combines strategic counsel with hands-on work: developing research submissions and briefing materials, preparing executives, and orchestrating cross-functional programs.
Responsibilities
Design and deliver programs that maximize influencer and customer awareness, consideration and recommendation of Stripe’s products and services globally, particularly for payments, fraud prevention, and agentic commerce
Build and maintain trusted relationships with key analysts across firms such as Gartner, Forrester, IDC, and coverage-specific firms
Craft clear, differentiated narratives aligned to market trends
Lead strategy, preparation, and execution of analyst evaluations and research cycles, ensuring high-quality submissions and effective cross-functional workstreams
Prepare senior leaders for high-impact analyst engagements with tailored insights and executive-ready materials
Synthesize analyst insights into actionable recommendations for product strategy and go-to-market alignment
Act as a trusted advisor to Stripe product and marketing leaders, providing expert guidance on market sentiment
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of experience in analyst relations, product communications, or a product marketing role
Proven results of managing analyst evaluations and research cycles, including submissions for major analyst reports
Demonstrated ability to drive results cross-functionally with product and marketing teams to develop clear, data-driven market-facing narratives
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including developing analyst submissions and briefing materials for senior executives
Ability to learn complex technical products and explain their capabilities, differentiation, and customer value accurately to external audiences.
This role requires approximately two weeks of travel per quarter.
Strong references from the analyst community
Preferred qualifications
Experience running executive communications and briefing preparation programs
Strong understanding of fintech concepts, trends, and industry dynamics

title: Government Relations Manager, AI
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Stripe is building the economic infrastructure that makes it easier for entrepreneurs and companies across the globe to grow their businesses. We are establishing a new function within our Washington, DC Government Relations & Public Affairs team and seeking an experienced professional with demonstrated expertise in Artificial Intelligence and policy advocacy to join our team and further Stripe’s mission. Stripes on the Government Relations & Public Affairs team operate in a fast-paced internal and external environment that requires collaborating with teams across our organization and with outside stakeholders. The culture is thoughtful, transparent, academically rigorous, and kind.
What you’ll do
As AI becomes central to how businesses are built and run, businesses like Stripe face a new set of questions: how infrastructure for AI should operate, what responsibilities sit at the infrastructure layer, and how to keep that infrastructure open, secure, and trusted.  We are seeking to work with a colleague who combines substantive AI-policy knowledge with the interpersonal skills to earn trust with policymakers. You will help officials understand the nuances of frontier technology and develop practical policy proposals that support innovation while addressing legitimate concerns about security, privacy, and misuse. This role will sit in the DC-metro area. We are not open to remote or travel candidates at this time.
Responsibilities
External Advocacy :  Establish trusted working relationships with congressional offices and administration officials across political parties.  Lead engagement with internal stakeholders alongside the Federal and State GR teams to recommend advocacy priorities for Stripe’s AI-policy portfolio, connecting developments in Congress and the executive branch to the needs of Stripe, and the businesses and developers they serve. Connect AI-infrastructure policy to Stripe's work in payments and agentic commerce, and share relevant US developments with international government relations colleagues. Keep clear records of engagements, decisions, and follow-up so the team can judge progress against its policy goals.
Policy Acumen: Examine Federal and State legislation, proposed regulations, and government guidance on model access, AI governance, privacy, cybersecurity, and accountability. Recommend specific changes and turn those recommendations into achievable advocacy plans. Working with the Policy team, this role will assist in the development of our positions on competition, interoperability, and access to proprietary and open-weight models, informed by the practical needs of developers and businesses of different sizes.
Strategic Leadership : Assess how national-security policy, export restrictions, cross-border data rules, and the treatment of models developed outside the United States could affect an AI platform offering access to multiple providers. Work with legal and technical colleagues to separate established requirements from unresolved questions. Recognize when an emerging controversy or government inquiry requires a rapid response. Bring together the right colleagues, establish the facts, and help leaders choose a proportionate course of action.
Collaboration:  Work with product, engineering, legal, privacy, security, and communications colleagues to understand operational realities before making policy recommendations or external commitments. Help the organization reach decisions when priorities differ. Find common ground with other companies, trade associations, researchers, and public-interest organizations. Build support for specific policy outcomes without losing sight of where interests diverge.
Thought Leadership: Write concise policy recommendations, meeting briefs, regulatory submissions, and executive preparation materials. Make clear recommendations on decisions or actions required.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
At least 8 years of relevant work in government, public policy, government relations, or technology advocacy, including meaningful responsibility for AI or closely related technology-policy issues.
A record of influencing federal policy through work in Congress, the executive branch, a technology company, or another organization engaged in substantive Washington advocacy. You should understand how decisions are made and how to move a proposal from analysis to action.
Personal credibility with officials and staff, supported by examples of earning trust, sustaining relationships, and working effectively with people whose political or policy views differ from your own.
Sufficient technical knowledge to discuss foundation models, inference, APIs, model and provider selection, and open-weight ecosystems with product teams and government officials.
Evidence of strong policy judgment: identifying what matters in a proposal, anticipating unintended effects, and developing alternatives that are technically workable and persuasive to government decision-makers.
The interpersonal range to brief a senior official, ask a careful question of an engineer, manage disagreement with a colleague, and maintain a productive conversation when the stakes are high. Listening, discretion, and dependable follow-through matter as much as presentation skills.
Writing style that helps people make decisions. You should be able to explain a complicated policy issue accurately, distinguish evidence from advocacy, and make a clear recommendation without unnecessary jargon.
Familiarity with the issues most relevant to AI platforms: data protection, security, platform responsibility, model availability, competition, and national-security restrictions. You should also be able to develop expertise in unfamiliar areas as priorities change.
Curiosity about how developers and businesses use AI, an interest in Stripe's mission, and the humility to revise a position when the evidence changes. Experience in AI infrastructure, cloud services, or financial technology would be useful, but is not a substitute for strong policy and relationship skills.
The ability to work from Washington, DC and travel as needed for government meetings, team collaboration, and policy events.

title: Policy Lead, AI Infrastructure
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Policy team works to understand and shape the regulatory and political environment in which Stripe operates — advising on product and business strategy, developing Stripe's policy positions, and engaging with policymakers and regulators around the world. The Policy Development & Strategy team sits at the center of this work, connecting Policy to Stripe's product and business teams and ensuring the company can pursue a proactive, coordinated policy agenda.
Millions of businesses use Stripe as a core platform to build and grow their own businesses, and increasingly that means building with AI. As AI becomes central to how businesses are built and run, this raises new questions: how infrastructure for AI should operate, what responsibilities sit at the infrastructure layer, and how to keep that infrastructure open, secure, and trusted.
What you’ll do
We are looking for a public policy professional to define Stripe’s approach to these questions and carry it into the world. In this role, you will develop Stripe’s positions on the public policy issues raised by AI infrastructure and help set the principles behind how Stripe’s AI platforms are governed, including trust, safety, and supportability. You will engage policymakers, regulators, industry groups, civil society, and other partners on these issues, in partnership with Stripe’s Government Relations team.
The right person will be equally comfortable working through a hard policy question with Product and Legal teams, briefing senior leaders, and representing Stripe's position with regulators or industry coalitions.
Responsibilities
Develop Stripe's policy strategy for AI infrastructure. Identify existing and emerging public policy issues and develop substantive positions and priorities that advance Stripe’s interests and reflect our values.
Shape platform policy principles. Work with the cross-functional teams that own day-to-day enforcement to set the principles and frameworks behind platform governance, acceptable use, model listing, and escalation, while preserving the benefits of neutral and open infrastructure.
Drive cross-functional alignment. Bring Product, Legal, Comms, Risk, Operations, and Government Relations to shared positions and priorities, and advance work from open question to decision to external execution.
Advise the business on difficult policy choices. Identify emerging risks and opportunities, translate external policy developments into product and business-model implications, and make recommendations on launches, supportability questions, public commitments, and other high-stakes decisions.
Develop Stripe's external policy positions. Turn internal policy work into external policy positions on AI infrastructure regulation in the US and globally: US AI policy at the federal and state level, national-security and export-control regimes, the EU AI Act, and emerging rules and standards for AI intermediaries and providers.
Engage externally on the substance. Engage policymakers, regulators, national security agencies, industry groups, standards bodies, academics, civil society, and other stakeholders to understand and anticipate policy developments; help build relationships and coalitions; and work with the Government Relations team to proactively shape policy debates.
Lead proactive public-policy initiatives and partnerships. Identify opportunities for Stripe to convene stakeholders, support research, develop industry frameworks, or partner with external organizations on difficult AI-governance and trust-and-safety questions.
Develop narratives and executive materials. Produce data-driven policy briefs, consultation responses, talking points, presentations, and executive communications that use Stripe’s data to turn technically and legally complex questions into clear positions for internal and external audiences.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
8+ years of experience in public policy, platform policy, trust and safety, technology policy, government, or a related field.
Strong policy judgment and a track record of developing positions on complex, contested issues where the legal or regulatory answer is not obvious.
Meaningful familiarity with trust and safety, platform governance, or online-service policy, including how policy choices translate into product and operational decisions.
Strong public-policy instincts and experience engaging policymakers, regulators, industry groups, or other external stakeholders.
Familiarity with AI policy and governance, and the range to engage credibly on fast-moving technical and regulatory questions.
Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional work across Product, Legal, Operations, Comms, and business teams.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce concise policy analysis and represent a position credibly with senior internal and external audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward building: this role will often require creating a position, framework, or external strategy where none exists.

About the team
In this role, you would join Stripe's Vulnerability Management team, whose mission is to "Surface vulnerabilities at scale across Stripe." By joining our team, you will have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach, securely.
Our vision is to create a culture of continuous excellence in managing vulnerabilities. We want to enhance customer trust by giving users context about threats and vulnerabilities affecting Stripe's systems. We aim to be a key partner in Stripe's risk management by providing visibility into vulnerabilities across Stripe's products and services.
What you’ll do
You’ll build the systems that identify and prioritize vulnerabilities across Stripe’s codebases, production infrastructure, and employee laptops. These collect software bills of materials (SBOMs) across tens of millions of lines of code, scan hundreds of thousands of hosts for package and kernel versions, and connect that inventory to known vulnerabilities (CVEs).
You’ll also build agentic systems to investigate emerging threats. For example, parsing breaking security news, identifying the technologies involved, and determining whether Stripe is affected.
Alongside this engineering work, you’ll help teams across Stripe understand their exposure, prioritize fixes, and drive remediation. The role combines building data pipelines and security automation with hands-on vulnerability analysis and security guidance for partner teams.
Since our systems interact with the entire Stripe codebase, you'll work in Go, Java, Ruby, and Python. The services we own are written in Go, so most of your hands-on work will be in Go. The typical balance of hands-on work is about 70% coding and 30% reasoning about security issues or providing guidance to partner teams.

Identify vulnerabilities using automated tools and triage them appropriately
Collaborate with other teams to drive remediation of vulnerabilities
Contribute to our overall security and risk management strategy
Continuously improve our security posture, processes, and tools

Familiarity with automated vulnerability identification tools and triage

About the team
Custom objects allow businesses to define custom data models in Stripe, ensuring Stripe reflects how their business operates. A business might have data that doesn’t fit standard Stripe objects, such as Shipments, Reservations, or InsurancePolicies. Once defined in Stripe, that custom data can be used with Stripe-native objects, such as Customers, Subscriptions, and Invoices. Companies can keep their existing system of record and bring over what their Stripe integration needs, or use custom objects as the system of record for that data.
Custom objects are the data pillar of Stripe’s extensibility platform, which consists of Stripe Apps, Stripe Workflows, scripts, and extension points.
We’re hiring a product manager to lead our custom objects product, which will make it easy for anyone to model, ingest, and use data on Stripe.
What you’ll do
This is a product management opportunity for an early-stage product (private preview!), and you’ll be responsible for the entire product line: identifying use cases, product design, iterating quickly by partnering with early adopters, pricing, and more. The intent of the role is to work closely with the production and facility engineering teams of the business, chemical SME, and chemical field technician to ensure that every chemical applied in the field is tied to a defined treatment objective — corrosion and scale control, flow assurance, H₂S management, or separation performance — and to a measurable, cost-justified outcome at the well, facility, and route level.
The role is intended to translate operating needs, production data, analytical results, and integrity findings into executable treatment strategies. As well as holding single-point accountability for program performance, vendor delivery, budget, data quality, and continuous improvement across the asset.
Serve as the single point of accountability for the Eagle Ford chemical program, including corrosion inhibitors, scale inhibitors, paraffin treatments, emulsion breakers, methanol, H₂S scavenger, biocides, batch treatments, and other specialty chemicals. Own the program from strategy and planning through field implementation, performance monitoring, optimization, and vendor management.

The role is accountable for cost forecast, budgeting, invoices and purchase orders, chemical-vendor performance, chemical usage optimization, program updates, and coordination of applicable MOCs and work-management activities.

Develop and maintain the Eagle Ford chemical-management strategy, annual plan, budget, performance targets, risks, and improvement roadmap.
Establish treatment philosophies and governance for continuous injection, batch treatments, H₂S scavenging, methanol, emulsion breakers, and specialty applications.
Use production conditions, chemical usage, analytical results, operating feedback, and integrity data to identify under-treatment, over-treatment, poor performance, and cost-reduction opportunities.
Maintain clear roles, escalation paths, decision rights, and handoffs among Program Engineering, Operations, Production Engineering, Facility Engineering, Integrity Management, Finance, Supply Chain, and vendors.

Maintain a closed-loop relationship with Integrity Management so corrosion-monitoring and inspection results inform chemical-treatment decisions, and chemical-program changes trigger reassessment where appropriate.
